scope: Publicly documented feature families, historical features, explicitly unresolved discovery items, and proposed browser foundations
evidence_policy: Only evidence_summary is a source-backed factual summary; contracts, architecture, schemas, and tests are proposed. No proprietary internals verified. No implementation tests executed.

features.title: Vertical sidebar and focus behavior
features.evidence_summary: Arc organizes tabs vertically.
features.rebuild_contract: Render Favorites, pinned items, folders, and temporary tabs as separate regions. Support resizing, collapse, keyboard toggle, edge hover reveal, scrolling, and drag targets. Preserve focus on the web page when merely revealing the sidebar.
features.state_and_storage: Persist width, collapsed preference, per-Space scroll position, and expanded folder IDs. Keep transient hover visibility separate from the saved collapsed state.
features.implementation: Use one tab store with a virtualized tree projection. Distinguish overlay reveal from docked layout so hovering does not reflow page content. Delay hide while a menu, drag, or rename field is active. Expose every row and section to accessibility APIs.
acceptance_tests: Collapse and reveal without losing text-field focus.
Resize at minimum width without clipping controls.
Scroll 1,000 tab rows while the active page keeps responding.
features.open_questions: Exact width limits, hover delay, and animation curves need platform observation.

features.title: Spaces and switching contexts
features.evidence_summary: Spaces carry separate tab organization and themes.
features.rebuild_contract: Create, rename, reorder, switch, and delete a Space. A switch changes the visible pinned tree, temporary tabs, theme, and selected tab. Support keyboard and gesture navigation. Deleting a Space must offer a clear destination or removal policy for its contents.
features.state_and_storage: Space(id, profileId, name, icon, theme, orderKey, selectedTabId). Each Space points to a browsing-data Profile; multiple Spaces may point to the same Profile.
features.implementation: Apply a Space switch as one transaction. Resolve the destination profile before loading pages. Restore selection and scroll without duplicating tabs. Keep a deterministic fallback if the selected tab has closed. Gesture previews must not commit history or change selection until the gesture completes.
acceptance_tests: Two Spaces in one Profile share the expected login.
Cancelling a swipe keeps the original tab active.
Reordering Spaces survives relaunch.
features.open_questions: Maximum Space count and exact gesture thresholds remain unverified.

features.title: Profiles and separate browsing data
features.evidence_summary: Arc profiles determine which Spaces share browsing data.
features.rebuild_contract: Create a separate work or personal identity, assign Spaces to it, and configure its search and archive preferences. Switching to a differently assigned Space changes the browser storage context before navigation.
features.state_and_storage: Profile(id, storagePartitionId, preferences, favoritesRootId). Cookies, HTTP cache, local storage, IndexedDB, service workers, permissions, history, and extensions belong to the partition or explicitly defined profile scope.
features.implementation: Create the engine context at Profile initialization. Never simulate isolation by clearing cookies during a switch. Moving a URL across profiles creates a new navigation in the destination; it cannot transfer an authenticated live renderer. Rename profiles without renaming or recreating their underlying storage directories.
acceptance_tests: Sign into different test accounts at one origin in two Profiles and verify isolation.
Rename a Profile without losing cookies.
Move a tab across Profiles without transferring session tokens.
features.open_questions: Audit the exact sharing scope of passwords, bookmarks, and permissions in the selected build.

features.title: Favorites as persistent icon tabs
features.evidence_summary: Favorites become icon-only pins when imported into Dia.
features.rebuild_contract: Offer small icon launchers for frequently used sites. Opening a Favorite activates or creates its page. Closing its loaded page should preserve the saved launcher. Provide un-favorite, rename, icon customization, and return-to-home actions.
features.state_and_storage: SavedTab(homeUrl, titleOverride, iconOverride, profileId, favoriteOrder) plus optional runtimeTabId. The saved URL and current navigation URL must be independent.
features.implementation: Keep favorite ownership at Profile level and project it into associated Spaces. Lazily create renderers and release inactive ones under memory pressure. Preserve custom titles instead of replacing them on page-title updates. Offer an explicit remove command distinct from unload.
acceptance_tests: Navigate a Favorite away from its home URL, close it, and verify the saved launcher survives.
Share Favorites across two Spaces using one Profile.
Keep separate Favorites in an unrelated Profile.
features.open_questions: Historical limits varied; do not enforce an unobserved fixed number.

features.title: Pinned tabs and pinned URL recovery
features.evidence_summary: Pinned URLs are editable; tabs can reset to them.
features.rebuild_contract: Pin a temporary tab into the durable section, optionally rename it, navigate within it, and return to its saved URL. Closing a pinned page and deleting its saved pin are different operations. Allow drag between pinned and temporary sections.
features.state_and_storage: Pin(id, spaceId, homeUrl, displayTitle, customIcon, parentFolderId, orderKey) references an optional live Tab. Track whether the current URL differs from homeUrl.
features.implementation: Use explicit pin, unpin, unload, remove, and resetHome commands. The favicon can expose the reset action when away from home. Reset must handle pending form edits through the normal navigation guard. Editing homeUrl changes the future destination, not silently the currently loaded page.
acceptance_tests: Pin a redirecting URL, edit its base URL, relaunch, and verify the edit remains.
Close a loaded pin without losing the record.
Unpin it into temporary tabs without opening a duplicate.
features.open_questions: Confirm the exact modifier behavior for preserving the navigated-away page.

features.title: Nested folders and folder previews
features.platform: macOS; Windows; preview details need Windows check
features.evidence_summary: Arc supports nested folders; macOS has searchable folder previews.
features.rebuild_contract: Group saved tabs into folders, including nested folders. Expand inline or open a hover preview with a scoped search field. Drag tabs and folders between parents. Provide rename, open contents, move, and copy-links actions.
features.state_and_storage: Folder(id, spaceId, parentId, name, orderKey) with a single ordered children relation shared by folders and pins. Persist expansion separately from membership.
features.implementation: Reject self-parenting and cycles before applying tree edits. Use stable IDs when a folder moves. A preview is a projection of the same tree, not a duplicated list. Search can show matching descendants with their breadcrumb. Resolve large bulk-open requests through a queue with lazy loading.
acceptance_tests: Reject dropping a folder into its descendant.
Move a nested folder and retain child order.
Search a collapsed folder and activate a matching tab without expanding unrelated branches.
features.open_questions: Verify hover timing, preview nesting, and exact Windows support.

features.title: Today tabs and auto-archive
features.evidence_summary: Arc offers configurable automatic tab archiving.
features.rebuild_contract: Temporary tabs enter a Today region. After the configured inactivity interval, move eligible tabs to Archive. Pins and Favorites remain saved. Provide manual close, clear Today, and undo. Archive is a recoverable state rather than deletion of browsing history.
features.state_and_storage: Store createdAt, lastActivatedAt, archivedAt, archiveReason, spaceId, and previousOrderKey. Keep wall-clock timestamps distinct from monotonic session timers.
features.implementation: Use an injectable clock and batch archive commands. Recompute eligibility after sleep rather than firing thousands of stale timers. Exclude active capture, downloads, audible media, unsaved forms, and focused tabs in the proposed policy. Release renderers only after the archive transaction is durable.
acceptance_tests: Advance a fake clock past the threshold and archive only eligible tabs.
Reopen an archived tab in its prior Space.
Sleep and resume without archiving the focused form.
features.open_questions: Exact default duration, exemptions, retention, and reference clock need observation; safe exclusions here are proposed.

features.title: Archive browser and restore
features.evidence_summary: Archived Little Arc pages can be filtered separately.
features.rebuild_contract: Search closed items by title, URL, time, source, and Space. Restore one item or a selected group. A restore should recreate organization metadata when available and avoid overwriting a newer saved pin.
features.state_and_storage: ArchiveEntry(snapshot, closedAt, closeReason, sourceSurface, restoreDestination, expiryAt). Distinguish archive records from navigation-history visits and bookmarks.
features.implementation: Index titles and URLs locally. Use a restore transaction that consumes or marks the archive entry while creating a live tab reference. If its original Space was deleted, ask for or choose a visible fallback according to a documented rule. Expose clear archive separately from clear history.
acceptance_tests: Filter Little Arc records without hiding ordinary history.
Restore a tab whose original Space was deleted.
Undo a bulk close once, with no duplicate records.
features.open_questions: Exact archive retention and whether restored records remain searchable require verification.

features.title: Command Bar: navigation, search, and commands
features.evidence_summary: The Command Bar includes an action-search mode.
features.rebuild_contract: Open from the new-tab or location shortcut. Resolve typed input into URL navigation, search, open-tab switch, bookmark/history destination, or browser command. Show an explicit selected result and keyboard hints. Escape closes without navigating.
features.state_and_storage: Command(id, label, aliases, availabilityPredicate, execute). Suggestion(id, kind, score, destination, profileScope). Store query history separately from web history.
features.implementation: Run URL parsing first, then local indexed retrieval and cancellable remote suggestions. Rank exact open-tab matches predictably. Attach a request generation ID so late results cannot replace a newer query. Commands share handlers with menus, preventing divergent shortcut behavior.
acceptance_tests: Type quickly and verify stale results never overwrite the latest query.
Use a command that is unavailable in Incognito and see it disabled or omitted.
Switch to a matching open tab without duplication.
features.open_questions: Ranking weights, default result selection, and all aliases are not public.

features.title: Site Search and search-engine selection
features.evidence_summary: Site Search uses a keyword followed by Tab.
features.rebuild_contract: Typing a registered keyword and pressing Tab changes the command bar into site-search mode. Enter sends an encoded query to that site. Backspace at the empty query or Escape exits the mode. Settings support a default web engine per Profile.
features.state_and_storage: SearchEngine(id, keyword, displayName, urlTemplate, profileId). Keep the selected engine token separate from the free-text query.
features.implementation: Validate templates to require a supported URL scheme and one substitution marker. Encode the query as data, not as a raw URL fragment. Normalize keyword matching without breaking IME composition. Prefer explicit engine intent over a heuristic chat router.
acceptance_tests: Search for text containing ampersands, Unicode, and question marks without query injection.
Exit a keyword mode with Backspace.
Preserve separate defaults across Profiles.
features.open_questions: Which engines auto-discover and whether keyword editing is available on Windows need checking.

features.title: Recent-tab switcher and tab shortcuts
features.evidence_summary: Arc’s switcher presents five recent tabs.
features.rebuild_contract: Holding the switch modifier reveals an MRU list; repeated presses cycle through it. Releasing commits selection. A quick press returns to the prior tab. Keep ordinal sidebar shortcuts distinct from recent-use order.
features.state_and_storage: Maintain a per-window or per-workspace MRU ring plus a frozen snapshot while the switcher is open. Track highlighted candidate separately from committed activeTabId.
features.implementation: Do not reorder the MRU ring as the user previews candidates; commit only on release. If a candidate closes, select its nearest surviving neighbor. Support reverse traversal and accessible labels with title and domain.
acceptance_tests: Cycle A→B→C and return to B using a quick toggle.
Hold the switcher open while one candidate closes.
Verify previewing candidates does not scramble cycling order.
features.open_questions: Cross-Space and cross-window MRU scope must be observed on the target platform.

features.title: Split View and saved split layouts
features.evidence_summary: Arc documents horizontal and vertical splits, with four-pane handling.
features.rebuild_contract: Create a split by dragging a tab to a target edge or invoking a command. Resize dividers, focus a pane, navigate it independently, reorder panes, and remove a pane. A saved split remains a durable sidebar object.
features.state_and_storage: SplitLayout(id, spaceId, tree, focusedLeafId), where each leaf references a Tab or saved pin and each branch stores axis and ratio.
features.implementation: Layout independent browser surfaces; do not embed arbitrary sites in ordinary iframes. Clamp ratios to minimum pane sizes. Address-bar, history, zoom, find, and developer-tools commands operate on the focused pane. Collapse a branch when one child remains.
acceptance_tests: Change one pane’s URL without altering its neighbor.
Restore a saved split after relaunch.
Reject or gracefully handle a fifth pane in an Arc-compatible four-pane mode.
features.open_questions: Verify Windows orientation and pane-count parity; four panes is historical macOS evidence.

features.title: Peek link preview and promotion
features.evidence_summary: Peek previews links from saved tabs and can become a tab or split.
features.rebuild_contract: Open a link in an overlay above the source page. Keep the source intact. Dismiss with Escape, close, or outside click; promote with expand or split controls. Normal navigation within the Peek remains contained until promotion.
features.state_and_storage: PeekSession(openerTabId, ephemeralTabId, profileId, bounds, navigationStack, promotionState). Avoid assigning durable sidebar membership until promoted.
features.implementation: Create an actual engine web-content surface using the opener’s storage context. Trap keyboard focus within the overlay while retaining the opener focus target. Promotion transfers the existing surface and history instead of reloading. Route external protocols and downloads through normal browser handling.
acceptance_tests: Dismiss Peek and regain the opener’s scroll and focus.
Promote a partially filled page without losing its fields.
Ensure Escape closes the intended overlay and not the browser window.
features.open_questions: Exact same-origin/cross-origin trigger rules and modifier precedence require observation.

features.title: Little Arc and external-link windows
features.evidence_summary: Little Arc supports multiple windows and timed archiving.
features.rebuild_contract: An external link can open a compact browsing window. Let the user follow links, perform a quick search, close it, or move its page into a chosen full-browser Space. Maintain a visible destination/profile control.
features.state_and_storage: Window(kind=little, profileId, openerApplication, tabId, lastActiveAt). Save a promotion target separately from the ephemeral window.
features.implementation: Receive operating-system URL-open events through a broker. Apply link-routing rules before opening a renderer. Promotion should reuse the page where the engine permits; crossing a Profile boundary requires a fresh navigation. Track each Little Arc window independently for lifecycle and archive.
acceptance_tests: Open two external links and close one without affecting the other.
Promote into the correct Space.
Auto-archive an idle window and recover its URL from Archive.
features.open_questions: Default routing, quick-lookup hotkey, and compact-window dimensions remain observation tasks.

features.title: Air Traffic Control link routing
features.evidence_summary: Air Traffic Control applies link-routing rules.
features.rebuild_contract: Let users define ordered matching rules that choose a Space or opening surface for incoming links. Offer a rule tester showing which rule matched. A disabled or missing target falls back predictably.
features.state_and_storage: RoutingRule(id, enabled, priority, matchType, pattern, targetSpaceId, surface). Include an explicit fallback policy.
features.implementation: Normalize hostnames with a URL parser before comparison; never match domains by arbitrary substring. Evaluate a bounded rule set once per incoming navigation. Keep external application opens separate from user-initiated in-tab links. Detect routing loops when a target redirects or launches another protocol.
acceptance_tests: A rule for example.com does not match example.com.attacker.test.
Higher-priority matches win deterministically.
Deleting the destination Space leaves a visible invalid-rule state.
features.open_questions: The supported original rule predicates and routing precedence are unverified; this is a proposed robust rule engine.

features.title: Themes, icons, and sidebar personalization
features.evidence_summary: Space themes and custom tab icons are documented.
features.rebuild_contract: Choose a Space color, light/dark appearance, label, and icon. Let a tab retain its favicon or use a user override. Apply themes to the surrounding browser chrome while preserving page rendering and readable text.
features.state_and_storage: Theme(baseHue, saturation, lightness, mode, contrastVariant). Store semantic tokens, not only precomputed pixels. Store icon overrides independently from fetched favicons.
features.implementation: Derive colors through a token pipeline with contrast checks. Avoid retinting content or security indicators. Animate between themes using opacity or compositor-friendly properties. Respect system reduced-motion and high-contrast settings.
acceptance_tests: Switch between dark and light Spaces with legible controls.
Receive a new favicon without erasing a custom icon.
Use long names and emoji without clipping accessibility labels.
features.open_questions: Original color interpolation, gradients, and app-icon unlock conditions are not reconstructed.

features.title: Multi-window tab handoff
features.evidence_summary: Arc documented one loaded tab instance moving between windows.
features.rebuild_contract: Selecting the same logical tab in another window transfers the live view while preserving its navigation, form, video, and scroll state. Keep the source window in a valid state when its displayed surface moves.
features.state_and_storage: Separate logical Tab identity from RenderSurface ownership and Window selection. A live surface has one presentation owner at a time.
features.implementation: Use an ownership broker to detach and attach the surface atomically. The previous window displays a placeholder or an alternate tab according to the chosen policy. Coordinate split panes, modal dialogs, and capture ownership before transfer. Never serialize a page into HTML to imitate handoff.
acceptance_tests: Move a tab containing unsent text and retain it.
Transfer a playing video without creating a second audio stream.
Race two window selections and end with one owner.
features.open_questions: Exact fallback UI and cross-window sharing scope changed historically; reproduce a chosen version.

features.title: Video Picture-in-Picture
features.evidence_summary: Arc includes a Mini Player and audio fallback.
features.rebuild_contract: Detach eligible video into a floating player when leaving its tab. Offer play/pause, return to tab, resize, and close. Closing the floating visual can leave audio controlled from the sidebar, depending on the selected policy.
features.state_and_storage: MediaSession(tabId, mediaId, state, currentTime, volume, pipWindowId). Runtime media state stays with the renderer.
features.implementation: Prefer engine Picture-in-Picture APIs and media-session controls. Keep ownership of the original element and track its lifecycle. Cleanly handle navigation, element removal, full-screen transitions, monitor disconnection, and renderer crashes.
acceptance_tests: Leave and return to a video without duplicate playback.
Close PiP and expose audio controls when still playing.
Destroy the source tab and close its player.
features.open_questions: Auto-trigger exclusions, control set, and supported players vary by release.

features.title: Meeting PiP and share-this-tab controls
features.evidence_summary: Meet PiP includes chat; sidebar controls can change the shared tab.
features.rebuild_contract: Keep the call visible during browsing, expose available meeting controls, and indicate which tab is being presented. Switching the shared tab must update the capture target and badge together.
features.state_and_storage: CaptureSession(sourceTabId, meetingTabId, mediaTracks, grantedScope). Store meeting controls as capabilities, not assumptions about every conferencing provider.
features.implementation: Integrate with engine capture and Document PiP hooks where available. A site adapter may expose supported controls but must detect missing elements rather than blindly click coordinates. Returning to a share dialog foregrounds the correct meeting window.
acceptance_tests: Change the shared tab and verify remote capture uses the new page.
Stop sharing and remove the badge.
Move between Profiles without displaying a stale meeting control.
features.open_questions: Provider-specific controls and Windows parity need direct testing.

features.title: Audio mini player
features.evidence_summary: Sidebar audio controls can remain after closing Mini Player.
features.rebuild_contract: Show a compact controller for an audible background tab. Offer pause, resume, mute, and return to source. Multiple audible tabs need a deterministic active-session chooser or an expandable list.
features.state_and_storage: Runtime media registry keyed by tabId with metadata, playback state, and supported action set. Persist user mute preferences separately.
features.implementation: Subscribe to the engine’s audio and Media Session signals. Use debounced amplitude indicators only as decorative feedback; actual playback state must come from the media session. Treat a muted live call differently from a paused video.
acceptance_tests: Pause the correct tab when two sources are audible.
Mute without changing playback position.
Close the source and remove the controller promptly.
features.open_questions: The exact arbitration policy among multiple audio sources is unknown.

features.title: Live calendar preview and join countdown
features.evidence_summary: A favorited Google Calendar shows a countdown and Join action.
features.rebuild_contract: Surface the next meeting near its saved calendar tab. Hover can show an agenda preview; a direct join action opens the correct call. Provide logged-out, no-meetings, cancelled-event, and connection-error states.
features.state_and_storage: CalendarConnection(accountId, profileId), Event(id, start, end, timeZone, joinUrl, calendarId, revision), display preferences.
features.implementation: Use a provider adapter that normalizes recurring events and time zones. Refresh using incremental cursors or bounded polling. Schedule local display updates from event timestamps, and recompute after sleep. Validate join URLs against the event’s permitted links.
acceptance_tests: Handle a recurring meeting shifted by daylight-saving time.
Update a cancelled event before the reminder fires.
Join from the Profile holding the right account.
features.open_questions: Actual integration transport and supported calendar types are not inferred from the badge.

features.title: GitHub Live Folders
features.evidence_summary: GitHub Live Folders track authored and review-requested PRs.
features.rebuild_contract: Present a dynamic folder of relevant pull requests. Allow project filtering; update entries when PRs appear or complete. Keep fetched entries distinct from manually saved tabs so removing a view item does not modify a pull request.
features.state_and_storage: LiveFolder(provider, connectionId, query, itemsByRemoteId, cursor, lastRefreshAt). Each item has canonicalURL, title, state, and lastSeenRevision.
features.implementation: Fetch through an authenticated adapter, paginate, deduplicate by repository and PR number, and cache results. Display stale state when offline. Reconcile updates incrementally to preserve selection and scroll. Never infer successful merges solely from a disappearing local tab.
acceptance_tests: A newly assigned PR appears once.
Merge a fixture PR and remove it from the active queue.
Lose authentication and show reconnect rather than an empty success state.
features.open_questions: Trigger for initial folder creation and exact filter choices need matching to a release.

features.title: Boosts: visual website customization
features.evidence_summary: Boosts V2 supplies a visual site editor and sharing.
features.rebuild_contract: Offer site-specific color, typography, and layout adjustments with a live preview, enable switch, reset, and saved presets. A picker can hide selected elements. Revisit the site and reapply the chosen customization.
features.state_and_storage: Boost(id, ownerId, matchRules, styleTokens, cssRules, hiddenSelectors, enabled, version). Separate a published snapshot from the editable local copy.
features.implementation: Inject scoped CSS through a privileged browser service into the target document. Use an isolated picker overlay and generate selectors with structural fallback. Reapply on SPA route changes and late DOM insertions with bounded observers. Keep user CSS distinct from site CSS so disable removes it cleanly.
acceptance_tests: Apply a palette, reload, and retain it.
Disable the Boost and restore normal rendering.
Hide an element in a dynamic page without leaking observers or hiding unrelated pages.
features.open_questions: Exact visual controls and selector strategy were not observed; these are independent implementation choices.

features.title: Boosts: custom CSS, JavaScript, and gallery
features.evidence_summary: Legacy Boost editing and a Boost Gallery were documented.
features.rebuild_contract: Provide an advanced editor with syntax validation, per-site scope, preview, and rollback. Distinguish inert visual presets from executable scripts. Gallery installation should reveal the included capabilities before enabling them.
features.state_and_storage: Versioned BoostPackage(manifest, styles, optionalScript, allowedOrigins, integrityHash). Maintain original author and local fork identity.
features.implementation: Compile or validate edits before replacing the active version. Execute optional scripts in an isolated world with a narrow bridge. Do not assume that scripts shareable in a proposed clone were shareable in Arc. For a safe first release, allow public CSS-only presets and keep scripts local.
acceptance_tests: Reject a broken stylesheet without replacing the last good version.
Restrict a script to its declared origin.
Fork a gallery preset and preserve its original metadata.
features.open_questions: Arc’s historical JavaScript sharing restrictions and current gallery availability need evidence before claiming parity.

features.title: Easels: spatial canvas
features.evidence_summary: Easels support alignment guides and video embeds.
features.rebuild_contract: Create a canvas containing positioned text, images, link cards, captures, and supported embeds. Select, resize, arrange, pan, zoom, duplicate, undo, and delete objects. Keep canvas navigation separate from object dragging.
features.state_and_storage: Easel(id, title, viewport, ownerId); Node(id, kind, position, size, zOrder, content, style); asset references in a blob store.
features.implementation: Use retained vector/object state and a command-based undo stack. Normalize coordinates to canvas space. Virtualize offscreen nodes and downsample large images. Snap guides should compare edges and centers in screen-pixel tolerance while saving unrounded geometry.
acceptance_tests: Resize a multi-selection and undo exactly.
Zoom around the cursor without moving objects in canvas coordinates.
Reopen a canvas with offline assets intact.
features.open_questions: Complete tool palette and text-formatting options require historical observation.

features.title: Web captures and live capture cards
features.evidence_summary: Arc offers element-aware captures and full-page portrait captures.
features.rebuild_contract: Select a page region or recognized element, capture a still image, and copy, download, or add it to an Easel. An optional live card can revisit a source region to refresh its visual state.
features.state_and_storage: Capture(assetId, sourceURL, viewport, deviceScale, rect, capturedAt, optionalAnchor). A live card adds refreshPolicy and lastSuccessfulSnapshot.
features.implementation: Capture through the rendering engine at the correct scale; tile long pages under memory limits. Anchor live regions with a DOM signature plus fallback crop. Refresh in the same authorized Profile. Show a stale snapshot if the page changes or authentication is unavailable.
acceptance_tests: Capture a region on a 2× display without offset errors.
Export a long page without missing strips.
Keep a stale live-card image when its anchor disappears.
features.open_questions: Live-capture behavior, refresh timing, and sharing of authenticated captures are reconstruction questions, not established internals.

features.title: Easel collaboration, sharing, and export
features.evidence_summary: Easels had sharing permissions; export supports images and an HTML archive.
features.rebuild_contract: Invite viewers or editors, share a read-only link, revoke access, and export usable files. The proposed clone should show collaborator presence and preserve a local copy when offline.
features.state_and_storage: Document ACL(owner, editors, viewers, linkAccess), versioned operation log, asset ownership, export manifest. Shared links reference a specific document, not the entire Library.
features.implementation: Use a CRDT or revisioned operation service with server-enforced access checks. Local rendering must never imply editing permission. Export nodes and assets into a self-contained static representation; convert unsupported live widgets to labeled snapshots. Make revoked links fail on subsequent access.
acceptance_tests: Concurrent edits converge without losing an object.
A revoked viewer cannot fetch document assets.
Open an export without network access and see all exported content.
features.open_questions: Arc’s actual collaboration protocol is not public; this is a replacement design.

features.title: Arc Notes
features.evidence_summary: Arc Notes were deprecated with an export path.
features.rebuild_contract: For historical parity, supply a lightweight rich-text note as a sidebar item and split-pane companion. Support titles, paragraphs, links, lists, basic formatting, autosave, search, and portable export.
features.state_and_storage: Note(id, spaceId, title, editorDocument, revision, updatedAt). Use a structured document model and export adapters.
features.implementation: Reuse a mature editor with composition, accessibility, and undo support. Persist incremental changes locally and debounce full snapshots. Import/export through a validated format without executing pasted HTML. Treat note deletion as recoverable before permanent cleanup.
acceptance_tests: Type with an IME, undo, close, and restore without text loss.
Paste formatted content and retain readable structure.
Export links and lists correctly.
features.open_questions: The complete historical editing toolbar is not established here; this is a defined minimal reconstruction.

features.title: Library: downloads, media, and saved creations
features.platform: macOS; Windows has a different surface
features.evidence_summary: Arc release notes reference Library downloads, Boosts, and Easels.
features.rebuild_contract: Offer a searchable hub for downloads, captures, and authored content. Support preview, reveal in file manager, drag out, rename where supported, and remove. Distinguish removing an index entry from deleting its file.
features.state_and_storage: LibraryItem(id, kind, localPathOrObjectId, title, createdAt, thumbnail, availability). Index files without treating the index as the source of truth.
features.implementation: Use asynchronous file availability checks and bounded thumbnail generation. Observe external moves or show a missing-file state. When deletion is intended, use the OS trash/recycle service where possible. Dragging exports a file reference without also triggering its open action.
acceptance_tests: Move a download externally and show it as missing.
Drag a file into another app without launching it.
Remove an Easel without deleting an unrelated capture.
features.open_questions: Which Library sections existed in each release/platform requires verification.

features.title: Super Copy, Markdown links, and Share Quote
features.evidence_summary: Arc supports Markdown link copying and selected-text quote sharing.
features.rebuild_contract: Copy the current URL with an optional title, remove known tracking parameters under a conservative policy, or create a quote card from selected text. Preserve the original destination and provide direct plain-link copying.
features.state_and_storage: SharePayload(canonicalURL, title, selectedText, optionalImage). Track raw and cleaned URLs separately; keep transformations explicit.
features.implementation: Use URL parsing and a versioned denylist of known tracking keys, never remove arbitrary parameters. Escape Markdown titles and destinations. Generate quote images locally with bounded text and visible origin attribution. Do not publish private page content automatically.
acceptance_tests: Copy a signed URL without breaking its signature.
Escape a title containing brackets.
Share a quote with Unicode text and preserve attribution.
features.open_questions: Exact tracking-removal rules and site-specific quote exclusions vary; test against a chosen build.

features.title: Developer Mode and development conveniences
features.evidence_summary: Developer Mode added capture access and JSON formatting.
features.rebuild_contract: Offer a per-site development layout with full URL visibility, one-click inspection, capture, and development-specific actions. Keep the conventional developer-tools window available regardless of this visual mode.
features.state_and_storage: DeveloperSitePreference(origin, enabled, toolbarState), DevToolsSession(tabId, dockingState). Do not persist privileged debugging connections silently.
features.implementation: Wire toolbar actions to the engine’s existing inspection, console, network, responsive viewport, and reload APIs. Detect localhost and development origins as suggestions, not mandatory mode changes. A JSON viewer must escape text and cap large-file rendering.
acceptance_tests: Inspect the focused split pane.
Render malicious JSON strings as text.
Close DevTools and confirm its background resources are released.
features.open_questions: The complete historical Developer Mode toolbar and automatic detection rules are unverified.

features.title: Arc Max: Tidy Tab Titles
features.evidence_summary: Max can shorten titles when a tab is pinned.
features.rebuild_contract: On a pin action, optionally suggest or apply a concise title. Keep the website title accessible and allow an immediate undo or manual override. A slow AI response must never overwrite a later user edit.
features.state_and_storage: TitleProposal(tabId, sourceTitle, proposedTitle, inputRevision, acceptedAt). Store userTitle separately from generatedTitle and documentTitle.
features.implementation: Send minimal title/URL context, constrain output to plain text and a bounded length, and validate against empty or URL-like junk. Commit only if the pin and title revision still match. Cache by normalized source and model-policy version.
acceptance_tests: Pin a verbose title and get a useful short label.
Rename before generation finishes and retain the user title.
Disable Max and pin without any AI request.
features.open_questions: Original prompts, models, length thresholds, and opt-in migration are not public.

features.title: Arc Max: Tidy Downloads
features.evidence_summary: Max suggests clearer downloaded filenames.
features.rebuild_contract: Offer a readable name when saving a download while preserving its file type and allowing the original name. Handle late suggestions without losing a completed download.
features.state_and_storage: Download(originalFilename, proposedFilename, finalPath, suggestionState, userEdited). Keep content-type and extension validation separate from generated words.
features.implementation: Generate from a bounded title, URL, and safe metadata; avoid uploading a file body by default. Sanitize reserved names and separators, preserve trusted extension logic, and resolve collisions atomically. User edits always take precedence. Rename through the download manager rather than racing a direct filesystem move.
acceptance_tests: Suggest a name for report.pdf while retaining .pdf.
Handle two identical suggestions without overwrite.
Cancel generation and complete the original download.
features.open_questions: Which download types Arc analyzed and exactly when it prompted need observation.

features.title: Arc Max: 5-Second Previews
features.evidence_summary: Hover plus Shift requests a linked-page summary.
features.rebuild_contract: After the explicit gesture, show a small preview with loading, summary, source URL, and failure state. Dismissing or moving away cancels unnecessary work. Support opening the destination and optionally copying the summary.
features.state_and_storage: PreviewRequest(url, profileScope, contentHash, generatedAt, expiry, status). Scope any authenticated cache to its Profile.
features.implementation: Fetch through a safe content-reading service, extract main text, cap size and redirects, then summarize with source attribution. Do not execute remote page scripts in privileged UI. Cache successful previews briefly and label partial reads rather than hallucinating inaccessible content.
acceptance_tests: Preview a normal article without navigating the current tab.
Hover repeatedly and avoid duplicate requests.
Show an authentication failure rather than a fabricated preview.
features.open_questions: The name is not a guaranteed five-second latency SLA; exact delay and fetch policy are unknown.

features.title: Arc Max: Ask on Page
features.status: retired on macOS: August 28, 2025; Windows status unverified
features.evidence_summary: Ask on Page used Find; macOS later removed it.
features.rebuild_contract: Augment a page-find surface with natural-language questions. Keep literal find intact. Answers reference visible page content and optionally highlight supporting passages. Retain the query when switching between literal and semantic modes.
features.state_and_storage: PageQuestion(tabId, documentVersion, question, evidenceSpans, answer, status). A page navigation invalidates evidence positions.
features.implementation: Reuse the page extractor and citation registry. Retrieve relevant chunks before generation, answer only within the selected page scope, and show insufficiency explicitly. Resolve highlights through stable anchors with text fallback; never highlight an old document after navigation.
acceptance_tests: Find literal text without invoking AI.
Ask a question and cite a supporting passage.
Navigate during generation and avoid placing highlights on the new page.
features.open_questions: Do not treat its historical Windows launch as proof it remains enabled today.

features.title: Arc Max: Tidy Tabs
features.evidence_summary: The Tidy button organizes temporary tabs into categories.
features.rebuild_contract: Take the current temporary-tab set, propose labeled groups, and apply organization as one reversible operation. Keep this separate from the Clear or auto-archive action.
features.state_and_storage: OrganizationPlan(inputTabIds, inputRevision, groups, unassignedIds). A group contains existing tab IDs, never new model-created IDs.
features.implementation: Classify from minimal metadata, validate that each tab appears at most once, and reconcile tabs opened or closed during generation. Preserve user-pinned order. Apply through the same tab-group commands used by manual organization. Undo restores previous ordering and grouping.
acceptance_tests: Organize ten mixed-topic tabs with no omissions or duplicates.
Close one tab during classification and apply safely.
Undo the entire organization in one action.
features.open_questions: Minimum tab count, group names, and persistence of generated categories need observation.

features.title: Arc Max: Instant Links and Ask ChatGPT
features.status: documented; Instant Links behavior changed historically
features.evidence_summary: Instant Links opens search destinations; ChatGPT uses a command-bar shortcut.
features.rebuild_contract: Provide explicit actions to jump directly to a search result or hand a query to a signed-in chat site. Keep standard search available. Preview or clearly label when multiple destinations will open.
features.state_and_storage: NavigationIntent(kind, query, destinationURLs, profileId). Site-chat handoff is distinct from an in-browser model conversation.
features.implementation: For Instant Links, obtain ranked search results and validate each destination rather than trusting invented URLs. Bound the number of tabs and deduplicate. For a chat-site shortcut, use a supported navigation/input path and preserve the user’s authentication context; do not claim access to the chat provider’s private API.
acceptance_tests: A direct-result request opens a real result.
Ambiguous results fall back to a search page.
A signed-out chat site requests sign-in without losing the user’s question.
features.open_questions: Early multi-result behavior differs from later first-result behavior; choose a version explicitly.

features.title: Space/folder sharing and link bundles
features.evidence_summary: Arc exports Space structure and can copy folder links.
features.rebuild_contract: Select a Space or folder and export its titled links in stable order. Support plain text and Markdown, with an optional shareable read-only collection in the proposed clone. Export is a snapshot, not a live session sync.
features.state_and_storage: LinkBundle(version, createdAt, sections, nestedItems). Only include navigable URLs and explicitly selected document exports.
features.implementation: Traverse the ordered sidebar tree deterministically and escape titles. Offer a preview that shows exactly which links will leave the app. Preserve duplicate URLs when they represent different saved contexts. Do not include cookies, tokens, or hidden page content in a link bundle.
acceptance_tests: Export nested folders with readable headings.
Preserve custom titles containing Markdown punctuation.
Re-import the clone’s format without losing ordering.
features.open_questions: Published Space-sharing availability at the current sunset stage is not established.

features.title: TypeTravel coverage gap
features.status: named in official FAQ; behavior unverified
features.evidence_summary: The official FAQ names TypeTravel without explaining its behavior.
features.rebuild_contract: Do not invent a feature definition from its name. Treat this item as a discovery task: find its command, settings, release history, or a reproducible interaction in an appropriate Arc build before defining a clone contract.
features.state_and_storage: DiscoveryRecord(featureName, build, entryPoint, screenshots, actions, observedStateChanges, confidence). No speculative application database schema is asserted.
features.implementation: Search version-matched menus and bundled localization strings, then run a controlled before/after experiment on synthetic content. If the feature is absent, record that absence only for the tested build. Use REA to trace only the concrete entry point after identifying it.
acceptance_tests: A reproducible trace identifies inputs, visible outputs, and persistence.
A reviewer can repeat the trace in the stated build.
Unobserved behavior remains marked unknown.
features.open_questions: This feature is not implementation-ready. Its inclusion prevents a false claim of exhaustive verified coverage.

features.title: Historical extras: Reader Mode, previews, membership UI
features.evidence_summary: Reader Mode and GitHub previews were removed; membership UI existed.
features.rebuild_contract: Keep optional historical modules outside core parity: a distraction-reduced article view, service-specific favorite previews, account membership cards, app-icon selection, referral/unlock presentation, and release-note notices. Gate each by a chosen historical target.
features.state_and_storage: FeatureManifest(versionRange, platform, state), account presentation preferences, preview adapters. Retired modules remain migratable but disabled by default.
features.implementation: Use a content extractor for Reader Mode and sandboxed adapters for service previews. Treat account decorations as local presentation state unless backed by a real entitlement service. Do not counterfeit an entitlement or infer current service availability from an old screenshot.
acceptance_tests: A removed module is absent in current-parity mode.
Historical mode exposes only deliberately enabled extras.
Disabling a preview adapter leaves the saved tab usable.
features.open_questions: Exact membership visuals, all preview services, and experimental feature flags are not exhaustively enumerated.

features.title: Intelligent Command Bar and new-tab page
features.evidence_summary: Dia routes between chat and search with an on-device model.
features.rebuild_contract: Accept URLs, search terms, natural-language requests, open-tab destinations, and skill names in one composer. Display the selected action explicitly and allow the user to choose search or chat. New-tab artwork and profile colors surround this entry point.
features.state_and_storage: InputIntent(rawText, explicitMode, classifierScores, selectedSuggestionId, profileId). Store a restorable query draft independently from any submitted chat.
features.implementation: Use deterministic parsing for URLs and explicit commands before a small routing classifier. The classifier suggests a mode; it must not override an explicit choice. Cancel stale suggestions. Persist back-navigation query state and ensure Enter submits once even during asynchronous mode changes.
acceptance_tests: A URL opens as a page.
An explicit search remains a search despite a chat-like sentence.
Back from results restores the query and selected mode.
features.open_questions: Exact classifier weights, training set, and thresholds are not public.

features.title: Contextual chat beside a page
features.evidence_summary: Dia’s central interaction is conversation with browsing context.
features.rebuild_contract: Open chat while reading a page, or start an independent chat from a new tab. Keep a visible context indicator. Stream answers, allow follow-up questions, stop generation, copy output, and reopen prior conversations. Closing the panel should not delete the conversation.
features.state_and_storage: Conversation(id, profileId, title, messages, contextBindings, activeRunId); PanelState(windowId, tabBinding, width, visible). Keep chat identity independent from the panel hosting it.
features.implementation: Use a streaming event reducer rather than rebuilding the whole conversation per token. Bind each message to the context snapshot used for that turn. A tab switch may change the suggested next context but must not rewrite evidence for an earlier answer. Preserve draft text when hiding the panel.
acceptance_tests: Hide and reopen chat without losing a draft.
Switch tabs mid-answer and retain the original source attribution.
Stop streaming and keep the partial answer readable.
features.open_questions: Exact per-tab conversation attachment and cross-window panel behavior require observation.

features.title: Tab mentions and context attachment picker
features.evidence_summary: Tab suggestions rank open tabs, history/bookmarks, then past chats.
features.rebuild_contract: Typing @ opens a picker. Selecting a tab inserts a labeled token with a removable attachment. Prevent duplicate mentions, expose unavailable sources, and distinguish content explicitly selected by the user from merely suggested context.
features.state_and_storage: ContextRef(type, objectId, profileId, displayLabel, sourceURL, accessScope, snapshotId). Composer tokens store IDs rather than depending on editable display text.
features.implementation: Query permission-filtered local indexes first. Resolve tokens to immutable snapshots when a turn starts, and show loading/error states for each attachment. A closed tab may remain resolvable through a permitted saved snapshot, otherwise require reopening or removal. Never silently switch to a similarly titled tab.
acceptance_tests: Attach two tabs with identical titles and keep them distinct.
Already-attached items are not re-suggested.
Revoke access before submit and surface the failed attachment.
features.open_questions: Exact number of attachments and ranking weights remain unknown.

features.title: Mention an entire Tab Group
features.evidence_summary: A group mention attaches its tabs together.
features.rebuild_contract: Select a group in the mention picker and show the contained sources before submission. Allow removing individual sources from this turn without changing the actual group. Keep group membership changes after submission from altering an in-flight request.
features.state_and_storage: GroupContextSnapshot(groupId, groupRevision, orderedRefs, resolvedAt). Each included reference has its own extraction status and size budget.
features.implementation: Expand group membership at submission time. Deduplicate overlapping group and direct-tab mentions by stable tab/document identity. Apply per-source and total token budgets, with explicit partial-context disclosure. Do not summarize only the first tab while implying the whole group was read.
acceptance_tests: Mention a five-tab group and account for all five sources.
A later tab addition does not change the current turn.
A failed source is identified while other sources remain usable.
features.open_questions: Whether the current product expands nested imported organization is irrelevant: Dia groups are not nested.

features.title: Page understanding and structured extraction
features.evidence_summary: Dia documents out-of-process reading and improved iframe/shadow-DOM support.
features.rebuild_contract: Read authorized page content into usable text and structured elements. Include tables, headings, links, selected passages, and supported embedded frames. Explain when content is inaccessible, virtualized, stale, or only partly read.
features.state_and_storage: PageSnapshot(id, tabId, documentId, url, title, capturedAt, blocks, sourceMap, coverage, failures). Each block retains frame identity and source anchors.
features.implementation: Run conversion in a sandboxed utility/renderer process. Traverse permitted document frames through browser-level APIs; a normal page script cannot read arbitrary cross-origin iframes. Exclude credentials and hidden controls. Bound DOM traversal, image decoding, and HTML-to-text conversion. Use adapters or provider APIs for virtualized documents, with explicit completeness flags.
acceptance_tests: Read a test page containing shadow DOM and an authorized frame.
A giant malformed page cannot hang the browser UI.
Password input values never enter a snapshot.
features.open_questions: No proprietary extraction code was recovered; coverage and algorithms here are a replacement contract.

features.title: Ask on Page and selected-content questions
features.evidence_summary: Ask on Page preserves the source when opening answer links.
features.rebuild_contract: Let a user ask about the current page or a selected passage in a compact surface. Show an answer with supporting citations; allow expanding into full chat. Keep literal Find as a separate predictable action.
features.state_and_storage: PageQuestion(documentId, selectionAnchor, question, answerBlocks, citations, status). Capture the selection text and document revision at invocation.
features.implementation: Extract the current authorized document, retrieve relevant blocks, and generate a grounded answer. Highlight exact evidence only when anchors still resolve. New links open according to the chosen context-preserving behavior. If the page changes, retain the answer but label its source snapshot.
acceptance_tests: Ask about a highlighted paragraph and receive an answer scoped to it.
Follow a citation without replacing the original page.
Navigate mid-request without mixing two documents.
features.open_questions: Entry gesture, shortcut, and selection toolbar design require direct platform verification.

features.title: Page, video, PDF, image, and spreadsheet summaries
features.evidence_summary: Dia summarizes YouTube, reads broader Sheets content, and accepts PDFs.
features.rebuild_contract: Choose a source and request a summary, comparison, extraction, or answer. Identify the actual material read: transcript, PDF text, rendered diagram, workbook cells, or visible page. A multi-source comparison must preserve units and source distinctions.
features.state_and_storage: DocumentAsset(mimeType, byteHash, pagesOrSheets, extractionStatus, sourceLocation). Evidence locations include PDF page, sheet/range, video timestamp, or image region.
features.implementation: Route each type to a bounded parser. Use OCR or vision for image-only pages and label its uncertainty. Read all relevant sheets through an authorized adapter rather than assuming the visible grid is complete. For video, use available transcripts and timestamps; do not claim to have watched frames if only subtitles were processed.
acceptance_tests: Answer from a PDF diagram with a page citation.
Read a second worksheet rather than just the visible first sheet.
Report an unavailable transcript without inventing its contents.
features.open_questions: File size, page limits, encrypted PDFs, and video-language coverage need measurement.

features.title: Writing assistance, rewrite proposals, and insertion
features.evidence_summary: Dia provides writing proposals and requires review before insertion.
features.rebuild_contract: Select or supply text, request a draft or rewrite, and see the proposal in browser-owned UI. Offer replace, append, copy, and discard where applicable. Preserve the original draft until the user accepts a concrete result.
features.state_and_storage: TextProposal(targetTabId, documentId, fieldAnchor, originalHash, originalText, replacementText, status). Keep proposal revisions separate from the site’s editor undo stack.
features.implementation: Identify editable fields through stable accessibility or DOM anchors. Before insertion, verify the document and field still match the reviewed proposal. Use normal input events supported by the editor, and retain a reversible replacement record. Never insert into passwords, hidden fields, or an arbitrary focused control after a tab switch.
acceptance_tests: Rewrite a draft, reject it, and preserve the original.
Change the source text during generation and require conflict resolution.
Accept into a contenteditable editor and allow undo.
features.open_questions: Supported editors and exact acceptance UI are platform-specific.

features.title: AI form filling
features.evidence_summary: The Autofill tool can prepare form-field content from chat.
features.rebuild_contract: Read an authorized form, map requested information to visible fields, and present proposed values for review. After approval, fill the fields and leave final submission under the user’s control.
features.state_and_storage: FormPlan(documentId, fields[{anchor,label,type,currentHash,proposedValue}], provenance, approvedRevision). Track each field’s result separately.
features.implementation: Use semantic labels, input types, and accessibility relationships instead of guessing from screen coordinates. Reject password/payment secrets and hidden controls. Revalidate the form after review. Trigger input/change events appropriately; do not click submit as part of a fill operation. Stop if the target document changes.
acceptance_tests: Fill a synthetic contact form and leave Submit untouched.
Preserve a field the user changed after review.
Report partial failure when one field disappears.
features.open_questions: The original classifier and complete field exclusions are not public.

features.title: Email drafts and calendar-event preparation
features.platform: macOS documented; Windows connected tools vary
features.evidence_summary: Gmail and Calendar tools search, draft, and stage events.
features.rebuild_contract: Ask for an email reply, event draft, or availability comparison. Read authorized source context, prepare recipient/time/content fields, and show a concrete draft before any external effect. Distinguish local draft generation from saving a remote draft or creating an event.
features.state_and_storage: ActionDraft(id, provider, accountId, operation, payload, sourceRefs, revision, approvalState, idempotencyKey). Calendar values retain named time zones.
features.implementation: Implement typed provider tools with separate read, stage, and commit operations. Revalidate recipients, calendar ownership, time zones, and revision at commit. Use provider IDs and idempotency keys to avoid duplication on retries. Let users edit the draft before the final action.
acceptance_tests: Prepare a cross-time-zone meeting without shifting the intended local hour.
Retry a committed draft without creating duplicates.
Change recipients and invalidate the prior approval.
features.open_questions: Whether each provider writes through API or UI is not claimed.

features.title: Research, deeper reasoning, and model routing
features.platform: macOS documented; Windows general chat available
features.evidence_summary: Dia adjusts deliberation and can use fallback models.
features.rebuild_contract: Support direct answers for simple requests and a longer research mode for multi-source work. Show progress, consulted sources, and an optional quicker-answer control. Provider outages should preserve the conversation and expose a recoverable failure.
features.state_and_storage: RunPlan(mode, budget, allowedTools, contextRefs, providerPolicy), RunCheckpoint(messages, toolResults, status). Persist semantic progress, not an assumed private reasoning transcript.
features.implementation: Use a provider-neutral model interface with streaming, structured tools, timeouts, and cancellation. A router chooses a bounded plan from request complexity and explicit intent. On fallback, replay only committed context and results; never repeat external writes. Show concise reasoning summaries or tool activity supported by the provider.
acceptance_tests: A simple page question avoids unnecessary web research.
A provider timeout can recover without losing sources.
Switching models does not repeat an already-completed action.
features.open_questions: Current exact models and routing policy are service-controlled and not reconstructed.

features.title: Citations, source inspection, and tool activity
features.evidence_summary: Dia exposes source-reading progress and clickable citations.
features.rebuild_contract: Show which sources were read and link answer claims to those sources. Tool activity can expand into a concise list of operations and outcomes. Distinguish planned, running, completed, partial, and failed work.
features.state_and_storage: Source(id, canonicalURL, title, snapshotId, location, permissions); Citation(sourceId, answerBlockId, span); ToolEvent(runId, toolName, status, resultSummary).
features.implementation: Generate references through registered source IDs rather than trusting model-written URLs. Validate citation IDs before rendering. Keep source titles untrusted and escaped. Do not interpret generated HTML as browser chrome. A citation indicates evidence used, not a guarantee that the claim is correct; evaluate entailment separately.
acceptance_tests: Every rendered citation resolves to a registered source.
Malformed model links cannot execute script.
A failed read appears as failed rather than completed.
features.open_questions: Exact source-link normalization and progress ordering are implementation choices.

features.title: Rich answers, code, tables, charts, and artifacts
features.evidence_summary: Dia renders rich answers and can retrieve generated artifacts.
features.rebuild_contract: Render structured prose, lists, tables, code, and generated work. Let users copy text, save a file, revisit an artifact, and continue editing it through chat. Preserve a usable partial view while content streams.
features.state_and_storage: Artifact(id, conversationId, type, title, version, contentRef, sourceRefs, createdAt). Messages reference artifact versions instead of duplicating their whole contents.
features.implementation: Use a safe Markdown/AST renderer and a separate sandbox for executable previews. Validate artifact MIME type, cap resource use, and version every edit. Keep a stable table layout during streaming. Exports should use the same content model as the preview, with an explicit unsupported-element fallback.
acceptance_tests: Stream a table without repeatedly losing scroll position.
Edit an artifact and retrieve its previous revision.
A generated script cannot access browser cookies or native APIs.
features.open_questions: Exact supported artifact types and whether a chart is native or code-rendered need observation.

features.title: Reports from multiple tools and tabs
features.platform: macOS/Windows product-level claim; UI parity unverified
features.evidence_summary: Dia advertises reports synthesized from connected work sources.
features.rebuild_contract: Ask for a research or work report, choose scope and sources, and receive a structured, editable document with provenance. Support follow-up revisions without discarding the evidence behind unchanged sections.
features.state_and_storage: ReportPlan(question, sourceScope, outline, timeWindow), ReportArtifact(sectionBlocks, citations, revision, coverageNotes).
features.implementation: Separate retrieval, evidence normalization, outlining, drafting, and verification. Resolve contradictions explicitly instead of averaging incompatible facts. Attach timestamps to mutable work status. Check that numbers and names come from evidence; mark missing data. Export through a document renderer with layout validation.
acceptance_tests: Compare two conflicting project updates and identify the conflict.
Produce a report where every material number has a source.
Revise one section while preserving other sections and their citations.
features.open_questions: Exact report templates, delivery formats, and scheduling capabilities are not established.

features.title: Deck generation
features.platform: macOS/Windows product-level claim; detailed workflow unverified
features.evidence_summary: Dia advertises generating presentation slides from context.
features.rebuild_contract: Request a deck, specify audience and purpose, review an outline, and generate editable slides. Support rewriting one slide, reordering, speaker notes where implemented, and export. Keep source references attached to factual content.
features.state_and_storage: Deck(id, theme, slides, assets, sourceRefs), Slide(id, layout, elements, notes, revision). Use explicit slide and element identities for editing.
features.implementation: Generate a structured content plan before layout. Fit text to measured boxes, use consistent grids and typography, and validate overflow after rendering. Keep generated illustrations separate from factual charts. Use deterministic chart data and a real presentation exporter if editable PowerPoint is required.
acceptance_tests: Generate ten slides with no clipped text.
Edit slide three without regenerating every slide ID.
Export and reopen with editable text and correct aspect ratio.
features.open_questions: Specific deck editor controls and file formats are proposed requirements, not verified Dia details.

features.title: Reusable Skills and invocation
features.platform: macOS; Windows Skills documented in October 2026
features.evidence_summary: Skills package reusable instructions, steps, context, and output formats.
features.rebuild_contract: Create a named shortcut for a repeatable task, invoke it from the composer, supply any inputs, and run it using the current authorized context. Permit editing and duplicating a skill. A skill is a reusable definition, not permission to act on every connected service.
features.state_and_storage: Skill(id, name, description, icon, steps, inputSchema, contextPolicy, outputFormat, requestedCapabilities, version). Each run pins a skill revision.
features.implementation: Compile a skill into the same run planner as ordinary chat. Expand parameters as data, validate required inputs, and intersect requested capabilities with current permissions. Show the skill name/version in the run record. Do not mutate a saved definition when the user edits a one-off invocation.
acceptance_tests: Run one skill against two different tabs using the right context each time.
Missing required input gets a specific prompt.
A skill cannot bypass a denied tool permission.
features.open_questions: Legacy slash aliases and exact Windows editor parity need checking.

features.title: Natural-language Skill builder
features.platform: macOS documented; Windows custom Skills available
features.evidence_summary: The builder turns a short request into reviewable skill steps.
features.rebuild_contract: Describe a repeatable task in plain language. The builder proposes a name, icon, inputs, steps, tools, and output style. Ask only necessary follow-up questions, let the user edit the proposal, and save after review.
features.state_and_storage: SkillDraft(description, proposedDefinition, missingInputs, revision, validationErrors). Keep unsaved drafts separate from active Skills.
features.implementation: Generate strictly schema-valid definitions and resolve every proposed tool against the available registry. A tool name in model text is not a real capability. Run validation and optionally a read-only sample before saving. Store requested permissions without silently granting them.
acceptance_tests: Build a weekly recap skill with explicit date input.
Reject an invented tool.
Cancel the builder without adding a broken skill to the launcher.
features.open_questions: Exact follow-up strategy and generated prompt structure are not public.

features.title: Skill discovery, sharing, and gallery
features.evidence_summary: Dia documented trying shared Skills; sharing produces a public artifact.
features.rebuild_contract: Browse templates, inspect their steps and capabilities, try a skill on chosen context, and save a local copy. Sharing publishes an intentional version of the definition, excluding the user’s data and provider credentials.
features.state_and_storage: PublishedSkill(id, version, author, definitionHash, description, allowedMetadata); Installation(publishedVersion, localOverrides).
features.implementation: Validate downloaded definitions as untrusted configuration. Do not execute arbitrary bundled code. Separate one-time trial from installation and updates. A local edit creates a fork or explicit override. Publishing must preview the exact prompt text, since it may contain accidentally embedded private instructions.
acceptance_tests: Try a skill without permanently installing it.
Share a template without including its last run’s attachments.
Update a template without silently broadening granted permissions.
features.open_questions: The old /skills URL currently redirects to the home page; current public gallery availability is unresolved.

features.title: Personalization and custom response instructions
features.evidence_summary: Dia offered written instructions and a per-chat personalization switch.
features.rebuild_contract: Let users describe preferred tone, formatting, background, and writing style. Show whether personalization is active for a conversation. A per-chat neutral mode should disable these preferences for that conversation without deleting them.
features.state_and_storage: Personalization(profileId, instructionText, enabledByDefault, revision); ConversationOverride(enabled). Keep personalization separate from history retrieval and learned memory.
features.implementation: Attach the selected revision as user preference context at run start, below system constraints and explicit current requests. Apply length limits and show an editable preview. Do not silently derive sensitive traits or treat a style preference as factual knowledge about the user.
acceptance_tests: Turn personalization off for one chat while retaining profile settings.
A current request for a table overrides a general prose preference.
Switching Profiles cannot import another Profile’s instructions by accident.
features.open_questions: Current placement of settings and any sample-based style onboarding need observation.

features.title: Historical Memory and ChatGPT-history import
features.evidence_summary: Dia replaced saved Memory with on-demand context tools.
features.rebuild_contract: For historical parity only, model memory as reviewable summaries of prior activity, with per-site exclusion, individual deletion, and per-Profile enablement. Imported conversation history must be explicitly selected and distinguish user statements from generated answers.
features.state_and_storage: MemoryItem(profileId, sourceRefs, factOrSummary, createdAt, confidence, exclusionScope). Maintain deletion tombstones and derived-index lineage.
features.implementation: Use an opt-in extraction pipeline with a sensitive-site deny policy, source attribution, and cascade deletion. Historical behavior included site exclusions and import; the proposed current build should prefer source retrieval instead of silently maintaining a hidden fact store. Never revive deleted memories from a cached embedding.
acceptance_tests: Delete a site’s memory and remove its derived search entries.
Exclude Incognito data completely.
Import a user-selected archive without treating assistant output as verified user facts.
features.open_questions: Historical controls are supported by the separate 0.45.0 notes; do not ship this as a current Dia requirement.

features.title: Search browsing history, chats, and generated files
features.platform: macOS documented; Windows tool parity check
features.evidence_summary: Current tools search history, conversations, and artifacts on demand.
features.rebuild_contract: Answer requests such as finding a previously visited page or earlier draft using explicit date/title/domain/content filters. Show matches with dates and source type. Let the user open the original or attach it to the current chat.
features.state_and_storage: Separate indexes for HistoryVisit, Conversation, and Artifact, each carrying profile/access scope, canonical identity, updatedAt, and deletion state.
features.implementation: Use local lexical search with optional semantic reranking. Resolve relative date ranges in the user’s time zone. Search metadata first and read full content only when necessary and permitted. Apply access filtering before scoring so hidden documents cannot influence snippets or counts.
acceptance_tests: Find a document from yesterday in the correct time zone.
Delete a chat and remove it from retrieval.
A query in one isolated Profile cannot reveal another Profile’s history.
features.open_questions: Exact indexing strategy and whether all prior page bodies remain available are unknown.

features.title: Voice dictation
features.platform: macOS documented; Windows availability needs checking
features.evidence_summary: Dia supports streaming transcription and dictation across tab switches.
features.rebuild_contract: Start dictation explicitly, show a recording indicator, stream provisional text into the intended composer, allow typed edits, and stop or cancel. Keep dictated text as a draft until the user submits it.
features.state_and_storage: DictationSession(targetComposerId, locale, audioState, provisionalSegments, committedSegments, startedAt). Audio retention must be explicit and bounded.
features.implementation: Stream microphone frames to a chosen speech service or local model. Reconcile final transcript segments without overwriting typed text. Keep the target composer bound across tab switches. Release microphone and wake locks on every completion/error path, including app suspension.
acceptance_tests: Speak while typing a correction and preserve both edits.
Switch tabs without moving dictation into the wrong field.
Cancel and verify the microphone stops.
features.open_questions: Shortcuts, languages, and audio-processing location are not inferred from release notes.

features.title: Queued messages, steering, stop, and resume
features.evidence_summary: Dia supports queued messages and steering during an active response.
features.rebuild_contract: Queue follow-ups while a run is active, edit or reorder queued messages, and distinguish a normal queued message from an immediate steering request. Stop generation without discarding completed work; resume from a clear checkpoint when supported.
features.state_and_storage: Run(id, state, checkpoint, activeToolCallIds), QueueEntry(id, position, revision, deliveryMode), SteeringEvent(appliedAtBoundary).
features.implementation: Use an explicit run state machine. Deliver steering at safe boundaries and track in-flight tool completion separately from token streaming. Stop prevents new actions; it does not imply a remote operation already sent was undone. Resume consumes durable results and respects idempotency keys.
acceptance_tests: Queue three messages and execute in the edited order.
Steer during a read tool without losing its result.
Stop during a remote write and report its actual outcome before retrying.
features.open_questions: Exact semantics of immediate interrupt versus cooperative steering can change by release.

features.title: Connected-app framework and tool execution
features.evidence_summary: Dia chooses connected tools automatically and exposes connection controls.
features.rebuild_contract: Connect an app, select an account/workspace, inspect connection status, and let chat request permitted capabilities. Show tool progress, structured failures, reconnect paths, and separate review for external writes.
features.state_and_storage: Connection(providerId, accountId, workspaceId, profileScope, credentialRef, scopes, state); ToolDefinition(schema, effectClass, requiredScopes, version).
features.implementation: Implement provider adapters behind a typed gateway. Store credentials in an OS-backed secret store, not in chat messages. Enforce schema validation, pagination, rate limits, cancellation, and audit records. Distinguish denied, expired, unavailable, partial, and successful results. Resolve discovered tools dynamically but only from a trusted registry.
acceptance_tests: Expired authorization produces a reconnect action.
A paginated result is labeled partial until complete.
A model cannot call a tool outside the user’s granted scope.
features.open_questions: Do not infer undocumented internal endpoints or claim every provider has write access.

features.title: Connected-app capability inventory
features.status: documented provider list; detailed scope must be verified
features.evidence_summary: Listed apps include Slack, Google, Microsoft, Notion, GitHub, Jira, and others.
features.rebuild_contract: Implement provider-specific read/search/open adapters for Slack; Gmail; Google Calendar; Google Drive; Notion; Jira; Confluence; Amplitude; Granola; Loom; GitHub; LinkedIn; Linear; Figma; Teams; Outlook; SharePoint; and Zoom. Present each capability as available only when that provider returns the necessary scope.
features.state_and_storage: ProviderManifest(id, supportedEntityTypes, actions, authMethod, scopeMapping, paginationStrategy, status). Store external IDs alongside canonical deep links.
features.implementation: Start with coherent vertical slices: email search and draft, calendar lookup, document search/read, chat-thread retrieval, PR search/read, design-file lookup, and meeting transcript lookup. Normalize results without throwing away provider-specific provenance. Loom and Zoom can supply recordings/transcripts; existence of an app listing does not prove all possible actions.
acceptance_tests: Every installed provider has an explicit supported-action matrix.
Unsupported writes return capability-unavailable.
A deep link opens the exact workspace/account item.
features.open_questions: Ashby/Dropbox beta and Google Chat were mentioned in later release notes; beta state and tenant availability require a current connector inventory.

features.title: Accounts, workspace selection, and connection discovery
features.evidence_summary: Dia supports provider account/workspace selection and app discovery.
features.rebuild_contract: Show which account each connection uses, allow switching eligible accounts or workspaces, and suggest relevant unconnected apps. If automatic connection is enabled, clearly show which apps became connected and how to disconnect them.
features.state_and_storage: ConnectionBinding(profileId, providerId, accountId, workspaceId); DiscoveryCandidate(providerId, reason, dismissedUntil). Treat browser login and AI connector permission as separate state.
features.implementation: Resolve identity through provider-supported authorization and explicit scopes. On an account change, invalidate cached results and live groups bound to the prior account. Discovery can use local usage signals without transferring page content. Keep auto-connect an explicit setting, not a consequence of merely visiting a site.
acceptance_tests: Switch Google accounts and stop retrieving the previous account’s documents.
Disconnect a provider and revoke future tool access.
Dismiss an app suggestion without repeatedly reopening it.
features.open_questions: Exact auto-connection consent and provider eligibility require observation.

features.title: Proactive suggestions
