features.evidence_summary: Dia surfaces expiring contextual suggestions across windows.
features.rebuild_contract: Offer a small number of useful next actions based on authorized work context. Let users dismiss, inspect, or run a suggestion. A suggestion should not execute a workflow simply because it is displayed.
features.state_and_storage: Suggestion(id, trigger, contextRefs, proposedAction, createdAt, expiresAt, dismissedAt, profileId). Share dismissal state across the relevant windows.
features.implementation: Use a rule or model pipeline with a strict notification budget and deduplication keys. Revalidate source state before execution. Expire suggestions tied to cancelled meetings or completed work. Suppress distracting surfaces during calls, full-screen presentation, or sensitive interactions according to explicit settings.
acceptance_tests: Dismiss a suggestion in one window and remove it in another.
A stale meeting suggestion cannot launch the wrong event.
No suggested action performs a write until invoked and reviewed.
features.open_questions: Triggers, scoring, and suggestion frequency are not public.

features.title: Morning Brief
features.evidence_summary: Morning Brief combines calendar, inbox, and relevant work links.
features.rebuild_contract: Prepare a daily overview with upcoming events, items needing attention, and relevant references. Display the covered time window, connected sources, and any unavailable data. Let users open sources or ask follow-ups.
features.state_and_storage: Brief(id, profileId, localDate, timeZone, sourceWatermarks, sections, generatedAt, status). Store source coverage separately from the narrative.
features.implementation: Run a bounded background retrieval job under the user’s enabled settings. Deduplicate signals across email, calendar, and chat. Rank actions by declared criteria such as deadlines and direct mentions, not speculative importance. Cache a finished brief and avoid regenerating it on every window open. Handle offline and partially connected states explicitly.
acceptance_tests: Generate one brief for a local day across two windows.
A disconnected inbox is labeled unavailable.
Calendar changes before opening cause a visible refresh or stale marker.
features.open_questions: Delivery time, scheduling controls, exact ranking, and refresh behavior are not publicly specified.

features.title: Live Calendar and meeting reminders
features.evidence_summary: Calendar previews offer meeting links and just-in-time reminders.
features.rebuild_contract: Hover a calendar pin to see the agenda, select included calendars, and join an upcoming call. Show a reminder anchored to the right account/window with a readable time and event identity. Permit dismissal and avoid duplicates.
features.state_and_storage: CalendarSubscription(connectionId, calendarIds), Reminder(eventId, recurrenceId, fireAt, state, windowAffinity). Model event revisions and cancellations.
features.implementation: Normalize provider timestamps and recurrence IDs. Recompute reminders on time-zone change, sleep/wake, event updates, and account switches. Join actions use validated event links. Keep visual countdown ticks local; do not poll the provider every second.
acceptance_tests: A recurring event appears at the correct local time after DST.
An edited join URL replaces the old one.
Multiple windows display at most one active reminder per chosen policy.
features.open_questions: Google calendar selection is separately documented in 1.46.0; Outlook/Teams support varies by build.

features.title: Meeting Tab Groups
features.evidence_summary: Joining a meeting creates a group that collects related tabs.
features.rebuild_contract: Create a meeting-scoped group containing the call and relevant resources. Add links opened in the meeting context. Show remaining time near the end. When the meeting ends, convert the group into ordinary recoverable organization rather than destroying its contents.
features.state_and_storage: MeetingGroup(groupId, eventId, meetingTabId, startedAt, expectedEndAt, phase, relatedTabIds). Track inferred links separately from user-added tabs.
features.implementation: Associate a call with a calendar event using normalized join identity and time window. Apply link-provenance rules instead of placing every newly opened tab into the meeting. Handle ad-hoc calls, two concurrent meetings, reconnects, and events running long. Stop countdown animations under reduced-motion settings.
acceptance_tests: Joining one call produces one group even after reconnect.
An unrelated new tab remains outside the meeting group.
Ending a call preserves manually added resources.
features.open_questions: The exact relevance classifier and cleanup delay need observation.

features.title: Tab Groups, pinned groups, and restore
features.evidence_summary: Groups persist; closing pinned-group tabs can unload without deleting them.
features.rebuild_contract: Create, rename, recolor, collapse, expand, pin, move, close, reopen, and dissolve a group. Distinguish closing loaded contents from deleting saved membership. Support both top-tab and sidebar presentations without changing identity.
features.state_and_storage: TabGroup(id, profileWorkspaceId, title, color, icon, pinned, savedMembers, liveMembers, collapsed, orderKey). Dia-compatible groups do not nest.
features.implementation: Use one group state machine for both layouts. Unloading releases renderer resources while retaining saved member records. Dissolving returns tabs to the ungrouped region; deleting removes the saved container. Closed-group restore is atomic and deduplicates windows already displaying the same group where the selected policy requires it.
acceptance_tests: Close a tab inside a pinned group and retain its saved item.
Dissolve a group without closing its live tabs.
Restore a closed window with its groups and order.
features.open_questions: Current auto-pin and close behavior supersede some earlier releases; select a version explicitly.

features.title: Automatic grouping, names, icons, and link grouping
features.platform: macOS documented; Windows naming parity check
features.evidence_summary: Dia can name groups automatically and group command-clicked links.
features.rebuild_contract: Automatically group related browsing when the relevant setting is enabled. Generate a concise group name and optional icon, let users rename it, and stop overwriting a manual choice. Keep link-open disposition configurable.
features.state_and_storage: GroupingPolicy(enabled, groupBackgroundLinks, namingMode), GroupMetadata(nameOrigin, iconOrigin, inputRevision, userLocked).
features.implementation: Track opener relationships and explicit user grouping before invoking semantic classification. Generate metadata from bounded title/URL context. Validate output and preserve a stable name while the group is in active use. The original release used background-link gestures for grouping; do not globally change standard modifier behavior without a visible setting.
acceptance_tests: Open two related links and keep their origin relationship.
Rename a group manually and retain that title after adding a tab.
Disable automatic grouping and recover conventional background-tab behavior.
features.open_questions: Automatic naming update cadence, thresholds, and latest defaults need observation.

features.title: Manage tabs and groups through chat
features.evidence_summary: Chat can open/close tabs and organize groups.
features.rebuild_contract: Interpret requests such as closing duplicate tabs, grouping research, renaming a group, or opening selected links. Show the affected tabs and a reversible result. Destructive bulk operations should use a plan based on exact tab IDs.
features.state_and_storage: TabActionPlan(inputRevision, selectedIds, operations, undoSnapshot, scope). Operations use a closed enum, not arbitrary code.
features.implementation: Resolve natural-language targets to a visible candidate list. Validate IDs, profile scope, and current revision before applying. Call the same command handlers as manual UI actions. Opening links must use verified user-provided or registered source URLs; a model-generated string alone is not authorization to navigate.
acceptance_tests: Group three requested tabs without touching another Profile.
Close duplicates with a recoverable undo.
A stale plan cannot delete a newly created group with a recycled label.
features.open_questions: Exact review thresholds and which operations auto-apply in Dia are not established.

features.title: Profiles, linked data, swiping, and defaults
features.evidence_summary: Dia Profiles can share browsing data and support swiping.
features.rebuild_contract: Create workspaces with independent tab organization and optionally link their underlying browsing data. Switch in place through menus, gestures, or shortcuts. Show which Profiles are linked and which remain isolated.
features.state_and_storage: Workspace(id, name, color, storageGroupId, aiScopeId, orderKey). StorageGroup owns browser data; AI scope is independently explicit. Arc Space migration creates this distinction.
features.implementation: Do not use one profileId for every concern. A visual workspace can share a storage group while retaining distinct organization. Relinking or separating data requires a defined migration plan; changing a pointer alone can lose access or expose the wrong account. Cancel or rebind pending suggestions when context changes.
acceptance_tests: Two linked Profiles share expected site login while maintaining separate tabs.
An isolated Profile cannot see that login.
Swiping wraps consistently and does not leave stale search suggestions.
features.open_questions: Do not assume linked browser data automatically grants cross-Profile AI access; verify and define it separately.

features.title: Incoming-link rules
features.status: documented new feature; older FAQ conflicts
features.evidence_summary: Mac 1.56.0 adds rules routing incoming URLs to Profiles.
features.rebuild_contract: Configure matching rules for links launched by other applications. Resolve the destination Profile and show a clear fallback if none matches. Keep normal in-tab navigation independent unless a rule explicitly applies there.
features.state_and_storage: IncomingLinkRule(id, matchPredicate, priority, targetWorkspaceId, enabled), DefaultLinkTarget. Record the applied rule in a local diagnostic event.
features.implementation: Reuse the normalized URL-routing engine from A15 but target Dia workspaces. Apply rules before loading cookies or creating web contents. A user’s explicit destination selection overrides inferred routing. Protect against recursive external-protocol launches.
acceptance_tests: A work-domain link opens in the designated Profile.
A missing target produces the configured fallback.
A misleading subdomain cannot match a different domain’s rule.
features.open_questions: The migration FAQ says this is absent; the dated November 5 release is newer and more specific.

features.title: Top tabs, sidebar, Focus Mode, and themes
features.evidence_summary: Dia offers both tab layouts and a chrome-hiding Focus Mode.
features.rebuild_contract: Switch between horizontal tabs and a vertical sidebar without changing the tab set. Focus Mode hides controls and reveals them on deliberate hover or keyboard action. Persist layout preferences and keep split panes functional.
features.state_and_storage: WindowLayout(tabPlacement, focusMode, sidebarWidth, toolbarVisibility), ProfileTheme(palette, intensity, appearance). Keep user preferences separate from hover state.
features.implementation: Render both layouts from the same store. Position browser surfaces through a single layout coordinator to avoid seams during resize. Theme chrome using contrast-safe tokens and optional page color signals. Reserve drag regions that do not intercept text selection or control clicks.
acceptance_tests: Toggle layout and retain selection, ordering, and groups.
Open Focus Mode with a split and keep both panes accessible.
Relaunch and restore the chosen tab placement.
features.open_questions: Pixel dimensions, colors, easing curves, and hover thresholds require UI capture.

features.title: Favorites, named pins, home URLs, and custom labels
features.evidence_summary: Dia added named pins outside Favorites and groups.
features.rebuild_contract: Support compact favorite icons and titled persistent pins. Rename tabs, choose icons, return a pin to its base URL, and unload a saved item independently from deleting it. Distinguish a pinned tab from a bookmark.
features.state_and_storage: SavedTab(homeUrl, currentTabId, presentationKind, titleOverride, iconOverride, workspaceId, orderKey). Group membership is optional.
features.implementation: Reuse the saved-item/live-tab separation from A04/A05. Keep manual names stable through page-title updates and imports. Duplicating a saved tab should follow an explicit policy, typically creating an ordinary tab rather than a second permanent pin. Include pins in search.
acceptance_tests: Rename a pin, navigate, relaunch, and retain the name and base URL.
Return to home without deleting the pin.
Search finds pins as well as ordinary tabs.
features.open_questions: Exact keyboard shortcuts and hover controls differ by platform and release.

features.title: Split View with independent pane controls
features.evidence_summary: Dia splits can have independent navigation and bookmark bars.
features.rebuild_contract: Open a tab alongside the current page through drag, a split action, or supported modifier gestures. Resize and focus panes, navigate independently, close a pane, and restore a saved arrangement.
features.state_and_storage: SplitLayout with independent pane selection, navigation state, chrome tint, and bookmark-bar visibility. The layout references existing tabs instead of copying them.
features.implementation: Use actual browser content surfaces managed by a split layout tree. Dispatch back/forward, location, bookmark, reload, and chat actions to the focused pane. Display focused-pane state clearly for keyboard users. Keep drag targets large enough without intercepting page interactions.
acceptance_tests: Back navigates only the focused pane.
A bookmark opens into the intended pane.
Closing one pane leaves the other live and focused.
features.open_questions: Do not copy Arc’s four-pane maximum into Dia without observing Dia’s limit and orientations.

features.title: Tab search, overflow, recent switcher, and bulk actions
features.evidence_summary: Dia searches Profile tabs and exposes recent groups and remote tabs.
features.rebuild_contract: Find tabs across windows in the current Profile, switch by keyboard, inspect overflow, restore closed groups, and select multiple tabs for copy, move, bookmark, or close actions. Keep recency search distinct from sidebar order.
features.state_and_storage: TabIndex(tabId, windowId, workspaceId, title, URL, state), MRURing, SelectionSet, ClosedWindowSnapshot. Remote-device entries are pointers until opened locally.
features.implementation: Use stable IDs and a frozen MRU list during cycling. Filter before ranking. Multi-select supports range selection and toggles with platform modifiers. Bulk operations share a single undo unit. When an active tab scrolls out of view, a compact indicator can retain orientation.
acceptance_tests: Search finds a tab in another window and focuses that window.
Copy selected URLs in a predictable order.
Restore a closed group without duplicating an already-open copy.
features.open_questions: Current switcher count is five per 1.51.0; exact inclusion rules require observation.

features.title: GitHub Live Groups and PR stacks
features.evidence_summary: Live Groups track PR work, with stack and status previews.
features.rebuild_contract: Show authored and review-requested PRs as a live work queue. Include state, checks, conflicts, unread changes, and optional collapsible stack relationships. Completed work leaves the active list but remains briefly discoverable through history or a completion view.
features.state_and_storage: LiveItem(remoteId, repoId, state, reviewStatus, checkSummary, stackId, stackPosition, readRevision). Persist collapsed stacks separately from provider data.
features.implementation: Use GitHub API/webhook or bounded refresh adapters with pagination and access checks. Reconcile by immutable remote IDs. Optimistically reflect locally initiated actions only when their actual outcome is confirmed. Do not confuse a tab closing with a PR being merged.
acceptance_tests: A changed review request updates the queue once.
Collapse a PR stack and preserve the state on relaunch.
Lose repository permission and remove cached confidential details.
features.open_questions: Provider pagination, stack metadata source, and precise completion animations are unverified internals.

features.title: Live Documents and work-activity groups
features.evidence_summary: Live Documents surfaces active Drive and Notion documents; Confluence was added.
features.rebuild_contract: Collect documents needing attention across supported services. Show recent comments, mentions, sharing activity, and unread indicators. Clicking an item opens the correct document rather than a generic app home page.
features.state_and_storage: WorkItem(provider, remoteId, accountId, canonicalURL, activityType, actorRef, updatedAt, readRevision). Group configuration lists included providers and workspaces.
features.implementation: Normalize activity events without merging unrelated documents that happen to share a title. Resolve a person’s identity from provider metadata rather than guessing from email addresses. Reconcile read state at event revision level. Use stale/offline indicators when refresh is unavailable.
acceptance_tests: A new mention adds one entry with a working source link.
Two same-named docs in different workspaces remain distinct.
Reading an item clears its badge without hiding newer activity.
features.open_questions: Ranking and exact inclusion rules are not specified publicly.

features.title: Tidy Tabs, cleanup groups, and empty-new-tab cleanup
features.platform: macOS; Windows current defaults need checking
features.evidence_summary: Dia documented temporary cleanup groups and later daily inactive-tab cleanup.
features.rebuild_contract: Offer cleanup of inactive temporary tabs with a recoverable staging or Recently Closed destination. Keep pinned material safe. Also discard abandoned empty new-tab pages without deleting a typed draft.
features.state_and_storage: CleanupPolicy(enabled, inactivityThreshold, stagingDuration), CleanupBatch(tabIds, createdAt, restoreSnapshot). Track non-empty composer drafts as protected state.
features.implementation: Use an injectable clock and activity model. Distinguish elapsed wall time from time actively using the browser. Exempt capture, active forms, downloads, and user-kept tabs under the proposed policy. Release renderers when archiving; retaining metadata must not keep pages consuming memory.
acceptance_tests: Clean ten inactive tabs and restore them as a batch.
A new-tab page with text is preserved.
Pinned groups survive cleanup and inactive renderers are actually released.
features.open_questions: May release behavior and later FAQ differ; measure the selected build’s defaults and timing.

features.title: Media: PiP, stashing, Spotify controls, and site mute
features.platform: macOS documented; Windows media parity check
features.evidence_summary: Dia supports PiP stashing, Spotify hover controls, and domain muting.
features.rebuild_contract: Keep video or calls in a floating window, move it partly offscreen, restore it, and return to the source. A pinned music tab can expose playback controls. Muting a domain applies to current and future matching tabs.
features.state_and_storage: PiPState(bounds, monitorId, stashedEdge, alwaysOnTop), DomainMuteRule(profileId, normalizedDomain), MediaSession registry.
features.implementation: Use engine media hooks and OS window APIs. Keep an accessible restore handle within the work area after monitor changes. Domain mute uses normalized host policy rather than arbitrary URL substring matching. Support unavailable controls explicitly when a service changes its player.
acceptance_tests: Stash and restore a call on a multi-monitor setup.
Mute a domain and open a new tab from it silently.
Clicking the PiP source focuses the correct Profile and tab.
features.open_questions: Exact service-specific controls and subdomain mute scope require observation.

features.title: Meeting screen-share handoff and presentation indicators
features.evidence_summary: Dia can switch the tab being shared during a meeting.
features.rebuild_contract: Show a clear badge on the tab currently being presented and a direct way to share a different eligible tab. Preserve the call and visibly confirm the new capture target.
features.state_and_storage: CaptureSession(activeSourceId, initiatingOrigin, grantedCapabilities, meetingTabId). Presentation status is derived from the capture service, not from local UI intent.
features.implementation: Delegate capture switching to the engine’s supported flow. Keep the browser indicator synchronized with the actual media track. If a switch fails, leave the previous source visibly selected rather than showing false success. Suppress unrelated popups while presenting according to user preference.
acceptance_tests: A failed target switch leaves the old badge accurate.
Stopping sharing clears all presentation indicators.
A captured tab cannot be silently replaced by chat navigation.
features.open_questions: Supported meeting providers and system-audio handling need platform testing.

features.title: Cross-device sync
features.evidence_summary: Dia syncs profiles, saved browsing state, settings, extensions, and remote-tab access.
features.rebuild_contract: Enable sync, pair devices, choose supported categories, and surface remote tabs without duplicating them into every local window. Keep organization, extension preferences, and eligible settings consistent. Expose disconnected and conflict states.
features.state_and_storage: SyncEntity(id, type, version, tombstone, encryptedPayload), Device(id, publicKey, lastSeen), RemoteTabSnapshot. Local runtime surfaces never sync.
features.implementation: Use end-to-end encryption with a documented recovery flow. Reconcile ordered lists through stable order keys and deterministic conflict resolution. Tombstones prevent removed groups from reappearing. A remote live tab is a URL/session metadata reference, not a transferable renderer or cookies unless a separately supported category exists.
acceptance_tests: Rename and reorder offline on two devices and converge deterministically.
Delete a group without resurrection.
Open a remote tab locally without closing it remotely.
features.open_questions: Exact cryptography, key recovery, category coverage, and conflict semantics are not public.

features.title: Arc/Chrome migration and portable export
features.evidence_summary: Arc import maps Spaces to Profiles and flattens nested folders into groups.
features.rebuild_contract: Offer a preview of source profiles, categories, and destination structure. Preserve titles, order, themes, pins, and supported browser data. Import by copy, retain the source unchanged, and report unsupported categories explicitly.
features.state_and_storage: ImportJob(sourceVersion, selectedCategories, mapping, checkpoints, warnings), SourceIdMap, ImportedRecord provenance. Keep payment/autofill omissions visible where matching Dia behavior.
features.implementation: Read a consistent supported snapshot or ask the source app to release locked files. Use versioned adapters rather than editing its live database. Map shared source Profiles into shared storage groups. Flatten nested folders with breadcrumbs to avoid ambiguous names. Make retries idempotent and allow rollback of imported records.
acceptance_tests: Import two Spaces sharing one source Profile and preserve intended shared login.
Flatten two same-named nested folders without collision.
Retry after interruption without duplicate pins.
features.open_questions: Boosts/Easels do not migrate; credential migration requires supported OS/provider access, not decryption bypass.

features.title: Extensions, side panels, and extension synchronization
features.evidence_summary: Dia supports extension side panels and no longer supports Manifest V2.
features.rebuild_contract: Install and manage supported Chrome extensions, pin actions, open popups/side panels, control per-site permissions, and keep enabled state and toolbar order in eligible sync categories.
features.state_and_storage: ExtensionInstall(id, version, profileStorageGroupId, grantedHosts, enabled, pinOrder, sidePanelState). Keep extension code outside the native privilege boundary.
features.implementation: Use the chosen engine’s actual extension system. A Chromium fork can preserve browser APIs; an Electron prototype cannot claim arbitrary Chrome Web Store compatibility. Resolve extension side panels independently from AI chat so closing one does not destroy the other’s state.
acceptance_tests: A Manifest V3 extension popup targets the correct profile.
A denied host permission is enforced.
A side-panel extension and AI chat do not overwrite each other’s state.
features.open_questions: Full compatibility requires a test matrix, especially native messaging, identity, capture, and store installation.

features.title: Privacy settings and AI permission boundaries
features.evidence_summary: Dia separates local storage, sync, AI processing, and optional content sharing.
features.rebuild_contract: Expose independent controls for AI access, connected tools, personalization, local data deletion, sync, and product-improvement sharing. Make context and external-action review visible in browser-owned UI.
features.state_and_storage: Policy(profileId, originRules, aiEnabled, telemetryConsent, syncEnabled), CapabilityGrant(runId, resource, effectClass, expiry). Deletion jobs track all derived caches.
features.implementation: Enforce policies in the privileged tool gateway, not solely in model prompts. Treat page text as untrusted data. Only registered source URLs can become navigations; target-specific write plans require reviewed content and revision checks. Propagate deletion through indexes and encrypted sync tombstones.
acceptance_tests: A malicious page cannot grant itself access to another tab.
Revoking a connector blocks a pending unexecuted write.
Deleting a source removes its derived retrieval entries.
features.open_questions: Do not translate vendor privacy promises into unverified guarantees about a new implementation.

features.title: Enterprise identity, SSO, and managed policies
features.evidence_summary: Dia documents SAML SSO, managed policies, and site-level AI restrictions.
features.rebuild_contract: Allow an organization to require an identity provider, restrict permitted accounts, manage extensions/settings, and disable AI processing on selected origins. Show managed settings as locked with a clear policy explanation.
features.state_and_storage: OrganizationPolicy(id, revision, allowedDomains, blockedOrigins, featureRules), ManagedIdentity, PolicyEvaluationLog. Keep user preferences as a lower-precedence layer.
features.implementation: Merge default, organization, profile, and user policies deterministically, with restrictive controls taking precedence where appropriate. Check policy at extraction, tool planning, and execution time. Use supported OS deployment profiles and signed configuration. Account identity and authorization remain separate.
acceptance_tests: A blocked work origin is excluded even when explicitly mentioned.
A managed extension rule cannot be bypassed by a local toggle.
A policy update revokes future processing without corrupting saved tabs.
features.open_questions: Exact MDM keys, admin UI, and deployment packages must be obtained from current vendor/admin documentation.

features.title: Plans, usage limits, trial, credits, and billing UI
features.status: documented commercial behavior; amounts not hardcoded
features.evidence_summary: Dia separates free browsing from metered AI plans and optional credits.
features.rebuild_contract: Show current entitlement, trial end, usage balance, reset time, and upgrade options. Exhausting AI allowance should pause AI while ordinary browsing remains usable. Credit auto-reload must be an explicit choice with visible spending controls.
features.state_and_storage: Entitlement(planId, validUntil, features), UsageLedger(eventId, taskUnits, cycleId), CreditLot(balance, expiresAt), BillingPreference(autoReload, limits).
features.implementation: Enforce metering server-side with idempotent usage events. Reserve budget before expensive work and reconcile actual use afterward. Keep prices and plan definitions in versioned server configuration. Handle payment failure, refunds, downgrade timing, and grandfathered accounts without deleting browsing data.
acceptance_tests: A retried request is not charged twice.
Running out of AI usage leaves normal navigation operational.
Disabling auto-reload prevents new automatic purchases.
features.open_questions: Current dollar amounts, rollout cohorts, and exact task-unit calculation are intentionally not assumed.

features.title: Search-first mobile launch and query entry
features.evidence_summary: Arc Search supports voice input and a normal-search/AI-search choice.
features.rebuild_contract: Launch into a fast query flow with a keyboard preference. Accept URLs, typed queries, dictated text, and external search intents. Keep ordinary web search available even when the AI service is unavailable.
features.state_and_storage: MobileSession(activeTabId, searchDraft, keyboardPreference, defaultEngine), QueryIntent(mode, text, source).
features.implementation: Build native keyboard and focus handling around a real platform browser engine. Resolve explicit URLs before search. Restore an interrupted draft after app backgrounding. Cancel stale suggestions and keep the bottom controls reachable with dynamic text and safe-area insets.
acceptance_tests: Launch with keyboard preference both on and off.
A voice transcript remains editable before search.
A failed AI request can fall back to normal search.
features.open_questions: Exact home-screen behavior and Android gesture parity need device observation.

features.title: Browse for Me answer pages
features.evidence_summary: Browse for Me creates structured answers with sources and follow-ups.
features.rebuild_contract: Submit a query, see research progress, and receive a readable answer page containing sections and source links. Suggested follow-ups expand the research. Allow editing the query and switching to conventional search.
features.state_and_storage: AnswerPage(id, query, locale, sections, sources, followUpGraph, generatedAt, status). Keep generated output distinct from ordinary visited URLs.
features.implementation: Search, fetch a bounded diverse source set, extract content, synthesize with registered citations, and render from a safe structured schema. Cache results with freshness labels. Handle conflicting evidence, missing sources, unsupported languages, and partial network failures. Do not fabricate sources to fill a fixed template.
acceptance_tests: A multi-source answer exposes the pages it used.
A follow-up adds relevant sections without duplicating everything.
A no-results query shows a clear failure or search fallback.
features.open_questions: Original source-count, ranking, prompts, model, and layout templates are not public.

features.title: Pinch-to-summarize interaction
features.evidence_summary: The reviewed current release notes did not verify the pinch gesture.
features.rebuild_contract: If recreating the remembered historical interaction, first validate it on a matching build. Proposed behavior: a deliberate pinch gesture summarizes the current page in a temporary card while preserving the page behind it.
features.state_and_storage: GestureState(scale, velocity, touchCount, activationThreshold), SummaryCard(documentId, sourceSnapshot, state). Keep summary generation separate from page zoom.
features.implementation: Use a gesture recognizer that resolves conflicts with accessibility zoom and normal page pinch-to-zoom. Start generation only after confirmed activation. Provide an equivalent menu command. Dismissing returns to the same scroll position. Reuse the grounded page-summary service rather than a separate uncontrolled prompt.
acceptance_tests: The summary gesture cannot trap users who need page zoom.
Dismissal restores reading position.
Unsupported or empty pages produce an explanatory state.
features.open_questions: Feature existence in the target build, exact gesture, UI, and retirement status are explicitly unresolved.

features.title: Call Arc conversational voice search
features.evidence_summary: Call Arc has been removed from Arc Search for iOS.
features.rebuild_contract: For historical reconstruction, offer a call-like spoken-search session with microphone state, streaming transcription, spoken answers, interruption, and follow-up questions. A gesture such as raising the phone requires independent verification before reproduction.
features.state_and_storage: VoiceConversation(sessionId, turns, audioRoute, listeningState, speakingState, interruptedAt). Store only explicitly permitted audio/transcript data.
features.implementation: Combine voice activity detection, speech-to-text, grounded search, and text-to-speech. Support barge-in by stopping playback while preserving the answered portion. Route sound appropriately for earpiece/headphones/speaker and release the microphone on backgrounding or termination.
acceptance_tests: Interrupt speech and ask a follow-up without overlapping audio.
Handle a denied microphone permission.
End the session and stop all audio capture.
features.open_questions: The old trigger, language set, and full UI are not verified; this is a historical replacement design.

features.title: Ads, trackers, and cookie-consent handling
features.evidence_summary: iOS cookie handling attempts rejection and leaves uncertain prompts alone.
features.rebuild_contract: Expose per-site and global controls for blocking advertisements/trackers and handling consent banners. Show blocked-item information where supported. A site-specific exception should be easy to reverse.
features.state_and_storage: BlockerPreferences(globalRules, siteExceptions, consentMode), FilterList(version, checksum), BlockStats(tabId, counts).
features.implementation: Use platform content-blocking facilities and reviewed filter lists. Consent handling should choose an actual supported rejection action, not merely hide an overlay and leave the page unusable. When detection confidence is low, leave the prompt for the user. Reload only after protecting unsaved page state.
acceptance_tests: Reject a supported consent dialog and keep page scrolling functional.
Leave an unknown dialog operable.
Disable blocking for one origin without disabling it everywhere.
features.open_questions: Filter-list providers and exact Android implementation are not established.

features.title: Mobile tab switcher, archive, and cleanup
features.evidence_summary: Arc Search includes a tab switcher and recoverable archive.
features.rebuild_contract: Browse a visual tab overview, activate or dismiss cards, open a new search, and recover recently archived pages. Automatic cleanup needs a visible duration setting and an undo path.
features.state_and_storage: MobileTab(id, URL, title, thumbnail, lastActiveAt, private, archivedAt), SwitcherState(selectedCard, scrollOffset). Thumbnails need a bounded cache.
features.implementation: Persist lightweight tab metadata independently from live WebViews. Keep only a bounded working set of loaded pages. Generate thumbnails asynchronously and avoid recording private content into shared disk caches. Handle app termination between a close gesture and persistence.
acceptance_tests: Close a card and restore its URL.
Relaunch after process eviction without losing saved tab order.
Archive metadata does not keep all WebViews alive.
features.open_questions: Default auto-archive interval and its active-tab exceptions must be measured.

features.title: Desktop Spaces and mobile synchronization
features.status: documented; sign-in/sync scheduled to end November 23, 2026
features.evidence_summary: Arc Search can access synced Spaces, pins, and active tabs.
features.rebuild_contract: Sign into an existing sync account, browse desktop organization, open a remote tab locally, and save a mobile page into the appropriate durable collection. Keep remote live sessions distinct from local tab instances.
features.state_and_storage: SyncedSidebar entities plus DeviceTabSnapshot(deviceId, tabId, URL, title, updatedAt). Device-local presentation remains local.
features.implementation: Use encrypted metadata synchronization with stable IDs and conflict handling. Cache enough organization for offline browsing but label remote freshness. Opening a remote tab creates a local instance; do not remotely close it unless the product explicitly supports that action.
acceptance_tests: A desktop pin appears once on mobile.
Open it offline and report unavailable content without losing the pin.
Concurrent edits converge without duplicated folders.
features.open_questions: Category coverage and mobile editing restrictions differ by version.

features.title: Sharing, exports, and selected-text actions
features.evidence_summary: Mobile export lists open tabs; iOS sharing can clean tracked links.
features.rebuild_contract: Share a URL through the OS sheet, send selected text to search, and export open-tab links. Generated answer pages and private tabs need explicit inclusion policies rather than silently joining a bulk export.
features.state_and_storage: SharePayload(URL, title, optionalText), TabExport(formatVersion, timestamp, entries). Maintain source and cleaned URL separately.
features.implementation: Use native share APIs, validate destinations, and conservatively remove known tracking keys. Escape exported Markdown/text. Export only selected browsing categories and exclude private content by default. Do not expose internal generated-answer URLs that are not publicly resolvable.
acceptance_tests: Share a normal link to another app.
Export tabs with non-Latin titles.
A private tab is absent from the ordinary bulk export.
features.open_questions: Browse-for-Me link sharing changed over time; do not assume historical shared URLs remain supported.

features.title: Mobile OS integration, widgets, app links, and handoff
features.evidence_summary: iOS notes document widgets, app-link preferences, Handoff, and PiP.
features.rebuild_contract: Support default-browser registration, home-screen entry points, open-in-app choices, system sharing, supported file downloads, and continuity. Preserve a user’s preference to remain in the browser rather than always launching a native app.
features.state_and_storage: OSPreferences(appLinkBehavior, widgetConfiguration, defaultBrowserEducation), HandoffActivity(URL, title, timestamp).
features.implementation: Use supported platform intents/universal links and lifecycle APIs. Detect whether a destination app is installed through allowed OS mechanisms. Avoid app-store loops. Handoff carries a URL and presentation metadata, not arbitrary browser cookies or a live page process.
acceptance_tests: Open a supported native-app link according to the saved preference.
A missing app falls back to the browser.
Handoff reaches the correct URL on the receiving device.
features.open_questions: Widget variants, shortcut integration, tablet layout, and Android app-intent parity require device verification.

features.title: Mobile privacy and standard browsing controls
features.evidence_summary: Arc Search includes browsing-data clearing, zoom, translation, and private-tab distinctions.
features.rebuild_contract: Provide Incognito/private sessions, history clearing, find, reload/stop, back/forward, page zoom, translation, downloads, and search-engine settings. Make private mode visibly distinct and keep it outside ordinary sync and AI history.
features.state_and_storage: PrivateSession(ephemeralStorageId), SitePreference(zoom, translation), BrowsingDataDeletionPlan(categories, timeRange).
features.implementation: Use an ephemeral engine data store for private sessions. Clearing history must not implicitly delete downloads or saved passwords without selection. Translation requests should make their external processing scope clear. Persist page zoom by the chosen site policy and reset it accessibly.
acceptance_tests: Private cookies disappear after ending the session.
Clear a time range without removing unrelated bookmarks.
Reset page zoom and return to 100 percent.
features.open_questions: The complete mobile settings list and exact translation provider behavior are not exhaustively observed.

features.title: Browser engine and process boundaries
features.evidence_summary: Chromium isolates browser and renderer responsibilities across processes.
features.rebuild_contract: Load real websites with independent navigation, storage, script execution, media, and crash handling. Browser chrome and tool execution remain outside untrusted page processes.
features.state_and_storage: BrowserContext, WebContents/TabSurface, FrameIdentity, NavigationEntry, RenderProcessHandle. Persist only logical state that can be restored.
features.implementation: For production Chrome-extension parity, evaluate a maintained Chromium-derived browser. For a prototype, Electron WebContentsView can host real pages but has extension gaps. Keep remote pages sandboxed with Node integration disabled. Use validated IPC methods and never expose a general filesystem or shell bridge to page content.
acceptance_tests: Crash a renderer without crashing every browser window.
A test page cannot invoke native filesystem APIs.
Two isolated storage contexts retain different cookies.
features.open_questions: No claim is made that Arc or Dia is an Electron app; local bundle inventory does not prove implementation language.

features.title: Tab state machine and command service
features.evidence_summary: This is a proposed implementation foundation, not recovered vendor code.
features.rebuild_contract: Provide create, activate, navigate, move, duplicate, pin, unload, archive, restore, and delete commands with clear semantics. Support multi-selection, groups, windows, and undo without duplicating business logic across UI surfaces.
features.state_and_storage: LogicalTab, SavedTab, RuntimeSurface, Group, Window, Workspace, UndoRecord. Runtime existence and saved membership are separate axes.
features.implementation: Validate commands against a current revision, commit database changes transactionally, emit events, and perform renderer side effects through a reconciler. If a side effect fails, mark it recoverable rather than rolling back unrelated user changes. Use unique IDs that are never recycled.
acceptance_tests: A close-on-pin unloads without deleting its saved identity.
Crash after commit and restore logical state on startup.
Bulk move is one reversible transaction.
features.open_questions: See the explicit state transitions in the architecture section.

features.title: Storage partitions, credentials, and private browsing
features.evidence_summary: Dia documents iCloud passkey support; the wider credential design below is proposed.
features.rebuild_contract: Keep isolated identities separate while allowing deliberate shared-data workspaces. Include password save/update prompts, a searchable credential manager, reveal/copy protected by OS authentication, supported password import/export, address/payment autofill, and platform passkey integration. Define private-session and profile-deletion behavior.
features.state_and_storage: StorageGroup owns cookies, cache, local storage, IndexedDB, service workers, permissions, and credential references. Workspace owns organization; AI scope owns retrieval permissions.
features.implementation: Use engine contexts/partitions and OS secret storage. Delegate passkey challenges to supported platform authenticators. Never send stored passwords, payment secrets, or private keys to the AI. Password exports need an explicit user-selected destination and plaintext warning. Private mode uses ephemeral stores and no persistent AI indexing. Sharing or separating storage groups is an explicit migration, not an incidental UI rename.
acceptance_tests: Cross-profile cookie and service-worker isolation holds.
Private browsing leaves no persistent history index.
Deleting one workspace does not destroy a shared storage group still in use.

features.title: Security, site permissions, blockers, and AI authorization
features.evidence_summary: Dia documents reviewed writes and restricted AI capabilities.
features.rebuild_contract: Provide camera/mic/location/notification/clipboard permissions, HTTPS/certificate UI, popup and external-protocol controls, content blocking, and a separate AI capability system. Denial must be visible and enforceable.
features.state_and_storage: SitePermission(origin, capability, decision, expiry), AIGrant(resourceScope, effectClass, revision), PolicyDecision. Origin includes scheme, host, and port.
features.implementation: Use engine security checks, site isolation, sandboxing, and signed updates. Gate AI reads and writes in a trusted service; page instructions cannot grant permissions. Restrict generated artifacts and external URLs through validation and allowlisted schemes. Include revocation checks immediately before effects.
acceptance_tests: A page cannot spoof browser-owned permission UI.
Revoked mic access stops capture.
A prompt-injection fixture cannot read another profile or submit a form without authorization.
features.open_questions: This design supports a safe clone; it is not a claim that every attack can be prevented.

features.title: Navigation and ordinary page controls
features.status: baseline browser scope; per-app UI not audited
features.evidence_summary: These controls are baseline requirements for a usable reconstruction.
features.rebuild_contract: Implement URL navigation, search, reload/stop, back/forward, per-tab history menus, zoom, find, print/PDF, translation where supported, file URLs, popup windows, error pages, and open-in-new-tab/window dispositions.
features.state_and_storage: NavigationController with committed and pending URLs, error state, back/forward entries, page zoom, and focused frame. Keep displayed security origin tied to committed state.
features.implementation: Delegate navigation to engine APIs. Respect downloads, external protocols, beforeunload prompts, redirects, and same-document history changes. Show failed and pending URLs accurately. Avoid disabling browser security to make difficult sites render.
acceptance_tests: Handle redirect chains without misleading origin UI.
Stop a load and keep a usable previous entry.
A beforeunload prompt protects an unsaved form.

features.title: History, bookmarks, Find, and local search
features.status: baseline browser scope; proposed data contracts
features.evidence_summary: Searchable browsing records underpin many Arc and Dia workflows.
features.rebuild_contract: Maintain visit history, bookmark folders, recently closed items, literal page find, and search across permitted titles/URLs. Keep these distinct: a visit is not a saved tab, and deleting history does not delete a bookmark.
features.state_and_storage: Visit(id, URL, title, visitedAt, storageGroupId), Bookmark(id, parentId, URL, title, orderKey), full-text indexes, ClosedItem snapshots.
features.implementation: Use SQLite or equivalent with indexed time and normalized URL fields. Record navigations only after the relevant commit policy. Exclude private sessions. Rebuild indexes safely from authoritative records. Find uses engine text search with match count, next/previous, case/diacritic rules, and accessible focus.
acceptance_tests: Delete a date range and update both history UI and AI retrieval.
Reorder bookmark folders and retain order.
Find cycles through matches without altering page content.

features.title: Artifacts, files, exports, and clipboard
features.evidence_summary: A common asset layer supports captures, canvases, reports, and exports.
features.rebuild_contract: Save and open user-generated documents, copy rich/plain content, export portable formats, preview supported files, and identify missing local files. Every export must have a usable output and clear scope.
features.state_and_storage: Asset(id, hash, MIME, byteLength, storageLocation, ownerScope), DocumentRevision, ExportJob(status, outputs, warnings).
features.implementation: Use content-addressed blobs and versioned metadata. Validate MIME and file size before parsing. Write exports to a temporary file then atomically replace the intended target. Sanitize filenames and embedded HTML. Preserve actual newlines in text exports and use platform clipboard formats deliberately.
acceptance_tests: An interrupted export never leaves a corrupt final file marked complete.
A missing asset has a visible placeholder.
Exported Markdown escapes titles and opens correctly.

features.title: Downloads and upload integration
features.evidence_summary: Downloads need their own lifecycle independent from the source tab.
features.rebuild_contract: Show progress, pause/resume where supported, cancel, save location, reveal/open, retry, and recent downloads. Support file selection and drag/drop uploads with user intent. Preserve original filename and origin metadata.
features.state_and_storage: Download(id, URL, originalName, targetPath, receivedBytes, totalBytes, state, dangerStatus, engineHandle). Completed history is separate from the file itself.
features.implementation: Use engine download hooks and native save dialogs. Prevent filename/path traversal and collisions. Retain resumable metadata only when supported by the server. Cancelling a paused download must actually release resources. Uploaded files are explicitly selected; AI attachment access is a separate grant.
acceptance_tests: Cancel a paused download successfully.
Two equal filenames do not overwrite silently.
Closing the source tab does not corrupt an allowed continuing download.

features.title: Keyboard, pointer, accessibility, and localization
features.evidence_summary: Shortcuts and accessible alternatives are part of feature parity.
features.rebuild_contract: Provide keyboard navigation, configurable shortcuts, context menus, tooltips, focus indicators, reduced motion, screen-reader semantics, high contrast, RTL text, IME input, and platform-correct mouse gestures.
features.state_and_storage: CommandRegistry, ShortcutBinding(platform, key, modifiers, context), FocusStack, LocalePreferences. Keep semantic actions distinct from key codes.
features.implementation: Route shortcuts through command availability predicates. Respect text editing and IME composition before global bindings. Test AZERTY, Dvorak, AltGr, and non-Latin input. Announce tab/group changes without excessive chatter. Every gesture-only feature needs a menu or keyboard equivalent.
acceptance_tests: Compose Chinese text without prematurely submitting.
Use all tab management features without a mouse.
Reduced-motion mode removes nonessential movement.

features.title: Operating-system integration and windows
features.evidence_summary: External links, window lifecycle, and native integration need platform adapters.
features.rebuild_contract: Register as a default browser, handle URL/file opens, manage window restore/fullscreen/multiple displays, provide OS menus, native sharing, and supported automation hooks. Respect each platform’s lifecycle.
features.state_and_storage: WindowPlacement(bounds, displayId, mode), ExternalOpenRequest(URL, source, disposition), NativeIntegrationPreferences.
features.implementation: Implement an OS adapter for macOS, Windows, iOS, and Android rather than spreading platform conditions through feature code. Validate external inputs. Clamp restored windows to an available display. Expose only documented automation operations, and keep incoming URL routing before page creation.
acceptance_tests: Restore a window after removing a monitor.
An external URL opens once in the intended workspace.
Fullscreen transitions retain input focus and correct window controls.

features.title: Media, calls, capture, casting, and device permissions
features.evidence_summary: Media surfaces require coordination with the browser engine and OS.
features.rebuild_contract: Support playback, PiP, full-screen video, camera/mic calls, screen/tab sharing, audio indicators, cast where supported, and return-to-source. Show active capture clearly and stop it reliably.
features.state_and_storage: MediaSession, CaptureSession, DeviceGrant, PiPWindowState. Runtime tracks must not be serialized into ordinary sync metadata.
features.implementation: Use engine/OS capture APIs and capability detection. Handle device changes, bluetooth routing, system sleep, permission revocation, and renderer death. DRM and proprietary codec support are separate engine/distribution requirements; do not claim universal streaming compatibility from basic HTML video success.
acceptance_tests: Remove a microphone during a call and recover visibly.
Stop sharing and end the outgoing track.
A renderer crash closes stale floating controls.

features.title: Provider integrations and background refresh
features.evidence_summary: Live folders, calendars, and AI tools can share provider adapters.
features.rebuild_contract: Authenticate supported services, retrieve authorized entities, refresh live data, and expose explicit failures. Separate background read refresh from user-triggered actions.
features.state_and_storage: ProviderAccount, SecretReference, RefreshCursor, CachedEntity, RateLimitState, MutationReceipt. Use account and tenant IDs in every cache key.
features.implementation: Implement retries with exponential backoff and jitter, bounded concurrency, incremental cursors, and pagination. Do not log credentials. Support revocation and workspace changes. Mutations require idempotency and a recorded result; retries must not duplicate emails/events.
acceptance_tests: A rate limit delays refresh without blocking UI.
Workspace switching invalidates the old cache.
Retry a mutation safely with a stable idempotency key.

features.title: Persistence, synchronization, backup, and deletion
features.evidence_summary: Reliable saved state requires migrations, conflict handling, and deletion propagation.
features.rebuild_contract: Persist state locally, recover from crashes, optionally sync encrypted records, export portable data, and delete selected categories consistently. Keep backups versioned and discoverable.
features.state_and_storage: Transactional local database, schemaVersion, append-only operation journal, SyncEntity versions, tombstones, encrypted blobs, device-key registry.
features.implementation: Use atomic transactions and tested migrations with rollback or backup. Encrypt sync payloads using a reviewed library and explicit key lifecycle. Define field-level conflict rules and stable ordering. Deletion removes derived indexes and schedules blob cleanup only when no retained document references them.
acceptance_tests: Crash during a migration and recover from a valid snapshot.
Concurrent offline edits converge.
A deleted record does not reappear when an old device reconnects.

features.title: Developer tools and extension compatibility
features.evidence_summary: Electron supports only a subset of Chrome extension APIs.
features.rebuild_contract: Expose engine developer tools, console, network inspection, responsive emulation, view source, task/resource diagnostics, and supported extension management. Declare unsupported APIs explicitly.
features.state_and_storage: DevToolsSession(tabId, paneId, docking), ExtensionCapabilityMatrix(engineVersion, API, result), DiagnosticsSnapshot.
features.implementation: Keep the engine’s developer tools integrated with the focused page surface. Test extension identity, storage, service workers, popups, side panels, native messaging, and host permissions individually. A prototype shell with unpacked extension support is not full Web Store parity.
acceptance_tests: Inspect the intended split pane.
Close DevTools and release its resources.
A representative extension suite reports exact supported and unsupported capabilities.

features.title: AI runtime, grounding, tool gateway, and evaluation
features.evidence_summary: A model-independent runtime supports the browser’s many AI features.
features.rebuild_contract: Run prompts with explicit context, stream output, call typed tools, record sources, apply budgets, stop/resume, and recover from provider failures. Ordinary browsing remains independent from AI availability.
features.state_and_storage: Conversation, Message, ContextSnapshot, SourceRegistry, Run, ToolCall, CapabilityGrant, Artifact, EvaluationResult.
features.implementation: Separate orchestration from model providers and UI. Validate tool inputs and outputs, apply origin/profile scope, and cache only within appropriate access boundaries. Treat all web/tool content as untrusted. Use structured output schemas for tab plans, filenames, and artifacts. Evaluate factuality, task success, denial behavior, cost, and latency on fixtures.
acceptance_tests: AI downtime leaves tabs and navigation usable.
Unregistered citations fail validation.
Tool results containing malicious instructions cannot expand permissions.

features.title: Settings, account lifecycle, updates, and diagnostics
features.evidence_summary: Settings and release management are necessary beyond visible tab features.
features.rebuild_contract: Provide searchable settings, per-profile defaults, account sign-in/out/deletion, import/export, update checks, release notes, feedback, crash recovery, and controlled diagnostic collection. Show which settings are managed or unavailable.
features.state_and_storage: TypedSetting(key, scope, default, migration, policy), AccountState, UpdateManifest, FeedbackDraft, ConsentRecord. Do not mix account entitlements with local workspace identity.
features.implementation: Use signed update packages and a staged rollout/rollback plan. Version settings and migrate renamed options. Diagnostics require explicit scope and redact secrets. Feedback must preview included logs/screenshots before sending. Feature flags carry platform/version metadata and an expiry/cleanup owner.
acceptance_tests: A bad update signature is rejected.
Signing out follows a defined local-data retention choice.
A diagnostics export omits cookies, tokens, and private page text.
